docs.title: Background NPCs
docs.text:
Populate Garry's Mod maps with civilians, police, bandits and medics. Actors walk, talk, react to danger and use vehicles when Decent Vehicle is installed.

Start with installation and first launch, then try the practical examples. If nobody spawns, follow troubleshooting.

docs.title: AI entry point: documentation maintenance
docs.text: Read this page, architecture, version history, and the affected source before editing. Root AGENTS.md points here.

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text:
1. Read git status, branch/HEAD, version.txt and bgNPC.VERSION in sh_init.lua. Preserve unrelated work.
  2. Compare release tags and commits through the requested version, then inspect subsequent commits present in the working tree. Separate a tagged release from later branch changes; never label dev behavior as released on Workshop.
  3. Code and load order decide contracts. Plans, old comments, MODLOG and an existing documentation page are evidence to verify, not proof of implementation.
  4. Check function definitions, every caller, realm guards, network receivers and optional-dependency availability. A sh_ prefix alone is insufficient to classify supported usage.

docs.title: What to update together
docs.text:
Change Documentation affected Public signature / return / alias Realm reference, method page, callers in examples and tutorials; preserve old URLs. Gameplay / default / command System page, settings/config guide, troubleshooting when relevant, history. File layout / loading / event flow Architecture and this maintenance map. New page EN/RU siblings, mkdocs.yml navigation + Russian label, index links. Release boundary History baseline, architecture version/commit, README and entry pages.

Use reference/server.md, client.md, shared.md as the API entry points. Explain authority and client snapshot limits. Record nil/NULL, argument defaults, validation, side effects, hook cancellation and entity replacement when relevant. Keep modern APIs primary and label actual compatibility aliases; do not invent a replacement for a missing method.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
• English: .md; Russian sibling: .ru.md. Keep both semantically aligned. Signatures and source paths stay literal.
  • Internal site links use .md even on Russian pages; i18n resolves the locale. Keep existing filenames/URLs and replace obsolete contents with a migration explanation.
  • Explain a system once and link to it. Keep rules/defaults on the owning page, implementation structure in architecture, historical differences in history.
  • Prefer small tables, runnable minimal examples and precise contracts. Do not add dependencies or runtime code for a documentation task.
  • Never include tokens, private machine paths, temporary bridge instructions presented as installation requirements, or unsupported performance claims.
  • Do not edit generated site/. Do not treat ignored planning files as shipped instructions.

docs.title: Validation and handoff
docs.text:
Install existing requirements-docs.txt if needed, then run python -m mkdocs build --strict. Check internal links, anchors, EN/RU navigation, source paths and documented signatures against the code. Review git diff --check and the complete diff. A docs-only change does not require launching GMod or running physics fixtures; explicitly say what was not verified.

Update the baseline only after reviewing the covered changes. Commit only the intended documentation/config changes when the user requested a commit. Push or deployment is a separate action; the site's existing workflow deploys master, not every local commit.

docs.title: Project architecture
docs.text: Source baseline: local 2.6.0, dev at 463d21ca (2026-11-14), plus the core engineering audit. Tag 2.5.1 is a7f2d9da; later branch behavior is recorded in version history. This describes the repository, not a promise that Workshop already contains these commits.

docs.title: Runtime boundaries
docs.text:
Realm Owns Entry points Server Population, bodies/brains, AI, navigation, damage, wanted/arrest, medics, vehicle providers sv_ files and server branches in sh_ Client Menu, voices/subtitles, ghost visuals, wanted HUD, route/debug rendering cl_ files and client branches in sh_ Shared Classes, configuration, API definitions, serialization and received actor records sh_ files; data is independent in each Lua realm

A shared filename says where a file loads. It does not guarantee a method can drive gameplay on the client. Use the realm references.

docs.title: Load sequence
docs.text:
lua/autorun/background_npcs.lua sends and includes background_npcs_core/sh_init.lua. The loader sorts files, loads sh_, sv_, then cl_ within each directory, recursively; explicit includes are deduplicated. Replic language files and menu option translations are loaded manually. tests/ is only sent to clients; bgn_selftest / bgn_selftest_cl include it when they run.

  1. Core: notices, classes, networking, utilities, scheduler, then remaining helpers.
  2. Built-in config/actors/phrases/states, custom config, legacy config adapter.
  3. Public API, cvars, commands, custom preload; save config defaults.
  4. Actor class/components/body adapters, events/update/sync.
  5. Navigation base/providers/IO, then the DV provider.
  6. Team and wanted modules, arrest module, remaining systems; brains, spawners, integrations.
  7. Menu languages/UI/debug; custom postload; BGN_PostLoadScripts.

Order matters: offender/state modules capture the registered arrest module. Reloading via bgn_scripts_reload reruns this loader; a map reload is the clean validation for changed bodies and persisted world state.

The shared UID allocator survives script reload; SERVER snapshot sequences use that same monotonic allocator. CLIENT retirement marks the actor removed before pending initialization can register it again. Scheduler ticks visit a snapshot of task IDs, so task removal/replacement cannot invalidate the live iteration. Long-lived services own their repeat loops; returning from a task finishes it. See audit contracts and limits.

docs.title: Files and responsibilities
docs.text:
All paths below are relative to the repository root. Under lua/background_npcs_core/:

Path Responsibility / connections sh_init.lua Version, shared storage, deterministic loading. core/ Class factory, task budget, network codec/chunks, cvar/command infrastructure, self-test runner (bgNPC.Test), notices, utility helpers. config/ Main settings; actors/ defaults and inheritance; states/ dialogue/scenic/arrest data; replics/language/ text and voice definitions. custom_modules/config, preload, postload Extension stages, also discoverable from separate addons through merged GMod Lua paths. api/ Actors/config/points/states/modes/vision/statistics/assertions and combat facade. compat/sh_legacy.lua retains old colon APIs. cvars/, commands/ Setting registration, defaults and administrative actions. actor/sh_actor.lua, components/ Character identity/health/lifetime and partial state, enemy, target, team, movement, weapon, animation, speech and vehicle methods. actor/body/ Server NPC/NextBot engine adapters. actor/update, events, sync Scheduled simulation, damage/death/save hooks, server snapshots and client binding. nav/ Provider facade, graph/A*, custom/navmesh/nodegraph providers; generator/ incremental route building, io/ editor/save/compile/dupes, legacy/ conversion. brain/fsm/, brain/goap/ State execution and combat planning. States call Actor methods; bodies perform engine actions. spawner/ Visibility-safe population placement/recycling, separate vehicle ranges, pursuit reinforcement and cleanup. systems/ Wanted/arrest, offenders, medics/corpses, teams/enemy sharing, gang wars/support/packs and combat cooldown, dialogue, seats, scenic, ghost crowd, modes. modules/ Optional integrations: DV, DarkRP, StormFox and NPC mods. dv/ owns provider access, traffic recovery, pedestrian detours, return and vehicle damage. ui/ Settings window, Classic panels, wizard/welcome, spawnmenu, update display, translations. debug/ Admin UID subscriptions and bounded decision/sight/signal journal (SERVER); cached mesh/HUD, camera and scene/hand markers (CLIENT); diagnostics and automated checks. tests/ Self-tests of pure logic, split by realm prefix (sh_, sv_, cl_). Not loaded with the addon: bgNPC.Test.Run includes them on each bgn_selftest (SERVER) / bgn_selftest_cl (CLIENT) run, so edited tests run without a map change. A test reads only public fields; a helper a test needs is exposed on its module with a read by tests/ comment.

Other repository paths:

Path Contents lua/entities/ NextBot actor and DV-related scripted entities/controllers; inspect each entity's init/shared/client files for realm. lua/weapons/ Tools, including route editing support. lua/autorun/ Addon bootstrap. lua/ulx/ Optional ULX administrative integration. materials/, models/, sound/, resource/ Runtime visuals, gang models/skins, voice assets and UI localization. tools/ Python regression checks, opt-in DV lab fixtures/bridge client, asset/voice generation helpers; not loaded automatically by the game. docs/, mkdocs.yml, requirements-docs.txt EN/RU site sources, navigation/translations, pinned documentation dependencies. .github/ CI/site deployment configuration. addon.json, version.txt, LICENSE, README.md Addon metadata, release number, license and entry page. site/ Ignored generated documentation; never edit by hand. quarantine/ Retained files outside the active loader; not an extension entry point.

Local planning/lab notes are not release contracts. Do not copy machine-specific paths or temporary bridge setup into runtime installation instructions.

On the first player spawn spawner/sv_pre_spawn_cache.lua warms resources: it creates and removes every configured NPC class/model and vehicle once. NextBot relationship sampling uses player dispositions without creating probe entities; see brains.

docs.title: Main relationships
docs.text:
config -> resolved Config cache -> per-actor config copy
navigation + player visibility -> spawner -> Actor registry
Actor -> brain (FSM / GOAP) -> state callbacks -> Actor methods -> body -> engine entity
systems/events -> reactions / wanted / arrest / medic calls -> state transitions
Actor <-> vehicle provider -> DV controller + chassis + seated visual
server Actor -> PVS snapshots + generation -> client registry -> UI / sound / rendering

The actor and UID survive vehicle boarding; its entity and body adapter do not. Registries, enemy/target references, wanted state and statistics follow the replacement. Addons must follow BGN_ActorEntityChanged(actor, old, new) for their own entity-local data. SERVER sends a player the snapshot identity only on first PVS sight or rebind, then only changed state, at most 8 snapshots per tick; a sequence number keeps a delayed identity packet from overwriting newer state on the CLIENT.

Door shelter is server-owned (systems/sv_door_hold.lua, brain/fsm/states/sv_hold_door.lua); GOAP chooses the action. Temporary knocked_down keeps the original entity and body adapter, hides/freezes them and uses a server ragdoll for physics and forwarded damage. The actor update loop runs only recovery while down; standing requires a free hull. Client synchronization/render optimization preserves the server's hidden-body flag.

systems/siege/ owns bounded NavMesh pocket detection, shared entrance reservations, siege positioning and special weapons on SERVER. GOAP selects siege; brain/fsm/states/sv_siege.lua executes its phases on both body types. Existing donor animations prevent native NPC throw/deploy events from producing duplicate weapons. Clients receive the ordinary state/animation updates. See room sieges.

systems/sh_carry_items.lua shares item definitions, model/animation checks and chance selection. SERVER owns real actors' item lifetime; body adapters exclude carried props from combat weapon queries. Only NextBot activity tables supply carrying locomotion. HL2 NPC movement is unchanged; CLIENT attaches briefcases to the hand bone on both body types; they never spawn physical drops. systems/cl_carry_items.lua manages real actors' client props from carry_visual in existing PVS snapshots. The newspaper hides the NextBot's driving parcel and fits the stock paper model between both hand bones. CLIENT also owns ghost visuals. Ghosts and actors materialized from them never carry items. Scenic placement remains SERVER-owned, including room/ledge traces, furniture bounds and atomic couch pairs.

debug/sv_scenic.lua owns admin scene placement, test ownership/Undo and the one-cycle GOAP door test. lua/weapons/gmod_tool/stools/bgn_scenic_debug.lua supplies the selector and live inspection HUD through the existing server-to-client Tool RPC. Manual placement validates the admin owner in both creation and delayed setup; only that path bypasses hidden-position checks. Normal spawner model hooks still decide all actor models.

docs.title: Configuration and stored data
docs.text:
systems/sv_lethal_weapons.lua owns the SERVER-only learned weapon cache and optional one-second perception timer. background_npcs/lethal_weapons.json is read once per server/map start; script reloads reuse the cache, and only a newly learned class rewrites the full file. See held weapons.

Cvar defaults are defined in cvars/sh_cvars.lua, sv_cvars.lua, cl_cvars.lua; registration and permissions are in core/sh_cvars.lua. Server settings are admin-controlled; client voice/UI options stay local. Actor definitions resolve inherit and @type references, cache the result and copy it on creation. After editing definitions, clear the config cache; existing actors retain their copy.

ui/spawnmenu/sv_spawnmenu.lua loads custom.dat at initialization/reload, rather than on entity creation, and clears the resolved config cache after mapping changes. Player spawns from the menu and Actor spawner Tool pass an optional owner to the common spawner: PlayerSpawnNPC can veto before creation, and PlayerSpawnedNPC provides gamemode accounting after actor creation. Automatic population passes no owner. Network framing and client upload limits are described in the audit.

GMod DATA paths are relative to garrysmod/data/, not this addon: background_npcs/nodes, graph, seats, compile (created by bootstrap), diagnostic background_npcs/test_report.txt. DV waypoints are separate from pedestrian routes. Preserve users' route files; legacy import/duplication conversion must not overwrite unrelated points. Compiled routes are Lua distribution artifacts generated from stored data.

docs.title: Development and verification
docs.text:
• Build and contribute: bilingual pages and strict site build.
  • Testing: diagnostics, Python/Lua regressions and opt-in vehicle fixtures.
  • AI documentation rules: scope, sources, realm contracts and maintenance checklist.

Unit/stub checks do not establish real GMod physics, multiplayer permission behavior or every optional-addon combination. Record exact conditions for live evidence.

Combat damage authority: systems/sv_first_attacker_found.lua receives confirmed engine/seated damage, records the pair initiator, evaluates existing-arrest harm and emits BGN_ConfirmedDamage for arrest initiation and witnesses. systems/arrest/sv_arrest.lua checks primary-officer compliance every 0.25 seconds. These records are SERVER-only; see wanted.

Damage entry points resolve siege payload ownership through Combat.ResolveVehicleAttacker(attacker, inflictor) before team/protection/reaction checks, independently of native damage-hook order. Actor search age comes from observed/shared timestamps, not NPC engine pursuit writes. Actors.Rebind transfers position/time and combat/recent-attacker references before updating the body's enemy. Siege entry excludes negotiation's hold_fire actors. See the combat continuation tree.

docs.title: Building the docs
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
python -m mkdocs serve

Open the address printed in the terminal. Before committing:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

English pages use .md; Russian siblings use .ru.md. Link to .md paths: the plugin resolves the selected language and falls back to English for missing translations. Preserve existing page paths for external links.

The workflow checks pull requests and deploys only on pushes to master. GitHub Actions needs write access, and GitHub Pages must serve the gh-pages branch. Local builds publish nothing.

Before changing public behavior, read AI documentation rules and architecture. Update both languages and the relevant realm reference with the code; preserve page URLs. See history for the baseline and release boundaries.

docs.title: Local Workshop build
docs.text:
On Windows, install Python 3.12+ and put glualint in PATH. Install the build dependency once:

python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-build.txt

Run build.bat from any working directory, or double-click it. The result is build/background-citizens/: a Workshop addon folder containing addon.json, the license, minified lua/ and copied game resources. build/ is ignored by Git. The build does not upload anything or change the source Lua files.

The first build downloads glua-minify at commit 4d19b690faf5e9cd3786d60609f6a02b6f645130 into build/.tools/, verifies its SHA-256, and runs it through Lupa's LuaJIT. Subsequent builds use the verified cache without downloading it again. The adapter fixes parser/scope issues for goto/labels, implicit method self, repeat-loop locals and global-name collisions.

Each Lua file becomes one physical line: comments and unnecessary whitespace are removed, local variables/functions/parameters receive shorter names, and multiline string values are preserved using escapes. Public methods, globals, table keys, paths and the SERVER/CLIENT/SHARED file layout keep their names. Comment-only files become return because GMad rejects empty files.

Repeated direct calls to selected standard math, string and table functions are cached in file-local variables. Calls through shadowed libraries are left alone; detected library writes/aliases or dynamic environment access disable the affected caching. Caching assumes other addons do not replace these standard functions after this file loads. GMod APIs and hooks remain dynamic. This is source minification with limited lookup optimization, not a promise of higher FPS or C++-style whole-program optimization. Debug stack traces lose source line detail.

Resources are copied from materials/ (vmt/vtf/png/jpg/jpeg), models/ (mdl/vvd/vtx/phy/ani), sound/ (wav/mp3/ogg) and resource/ (properties/ttf). Other extensions and Workshop-incompatible *.sw.vtx are excluded. The build folder is a standalone copy; rebuild to pick up changes.

Both source and generated Lua must pass glualint dump-ast. A failed transform or syntax check leaves the previous successful output intact. A successful rebuild replaces only build/background-citizens/, removing stale generated files. Other files under build/ are retained. Development tools, docs and quarantined files are not included. To update the Workshop item (id 2341497926), run publish.bat: it builds, packs build/background-citizens.gma with bin/gmad.exe, asks for the update description (empty cancels) and uploads with bin/gmpublish.exe (Steam must be running).

Build regression checks:

python.exe -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_build.py -v

These checks cover transformations and output handling outside the game; test the generated addon in GMod before publishing it.

docs.title: Core engineering audit
docs.text: Local changes against dev at cde2f701 (2.5.1, 2026-11-14); publication is not verified. Legacy was read as a historical reference and remains unchanged.

docs.title: Scope and decisions
docs.text:
The review followed the load sequence and module map: core services and public/compatibility APIs, actor components and both bodies, FSM/GOAP, navigation providers and route IO, population/vehicles, wanted/arrest, perception and team reactions, medics/corpses, siege/doors, scenic/carry/ghost systems, optional integrations, client rendering, debug tools and settings/spawn menus. GLua parsing covers the entire current core. Behavioral regression checks concentrate on the changed paths; this is not evidence that every map, engine callback or optional addon combination has been exercised.

Legacy's useful lessons are direct operations, small event handlers and explicit configuration. Its large actor base, repeated registry scans and dependence on SLibrary are not restoration targets. The current Actor → brain → body split, navigation providers, shared task budget and compatibility aliases remain. The body adapters have distinct engine responsibilities; the registries and old aliases have external users. Absence of a direct internal caller was not used as grounds to delete public APIs.

docs.title: Confirmed fixes
docs.text:
Area Problem and correction Mechanics Lua's and/or selection discarded explicit false. Boolean overrides now survive. The duplicate iNPC init hook is removed; actor initialization/rebind owns its flag. Recurring services Door passage, player observation and ambient coughs returned after one pass. Explicit loops now keep them alive, including an initially empty server. Looking away resets continuous observation. Scheduler Tasks changed the live order during iteration, skipping/repeating work. Each tick visits a snapshot of IDs once; new IDs start next tick, removals take effect immediately; replacing an existing ID can run its new task in the same tick. Identity/lifetime UID allocation and snapshot sequences restarted on Lua reload. The allocator persists and supplies sync sequences too. Client retirement marks the actor removed before delayed initialization can register it again; server entity removal stops its actor/brain. String UIDs get a numeric LOD phase without changing their identity. Navigation Empty random queries could fail or fall back outside the requested graph radius. They now return nil. NavMesh sampling indexes the actual area list, independent of area IDs. Reload navigation after editing the mesh externally. GOAP Counting unsatisfied facts overestimated the cost when one action changes several facts. The lower bound is now one action; goal conditions distinguish cache entries, and action registration invalidates cached plans. The 200-iteration search limit remains. Spawning Skin/bodygroup selection included invalid upper indices; the applied skin could differ from the hook-approved value. Indices are zero-based and the approved value is applied once. Player-owned menu/Tool spawns now respect the gamemode spawn hooks and ownership/counting; automatic population retains its existing rules. Configuration Spawnmenu read/decompressed custom.dat on every entity creation. It now loads at initialization/reload, invalidates resolved actor config after updates, and drops disconnected players' defaults. Regeneration/client Regeneration honors the configured interval/ceiling without reducing excess health. Client seat downloads use the active local tool, not a nonexistent server sender. Language sync sends only the language code. Network Invalid string/count fields, excessive nesting and inconsistent fragments are rejected. Client buffering/decompression is bounded; transfer/wait IDs persist across reloads. See the transport contract below.

Small removals include unused radius calculations, an unused entity lookup, GOAP's invalid bit-count heuristic, the duplicate iNPC hook, duplicate registry reset code and a second copy of the idle sequence list. The object scan no longer yields twice per candidate: it yields only when the shared budget is spent, retaining its 100-unit radius and one forward trace. It rechecks the body after event callbacks that may remove/rebind it. These changes remove demonstrable work; no FPS or percentage speedup is claimed.

docs.title: Transport contract
docs.text:
bgNPC.Net retains its message names, wire encoding, admin gates and nil argument handling. Both realms reject table nesting beyond 64 levels; callbacks accept at most 256 arguments. Chunk headers must agree on message name, compression and total; each part is at most 60,000 bytes and its index/length must match the packet.

SERVER accepts at most eight incomplete transfers and 8 MiB of buffered fragments per client, and at most 32 MiB after decompression per message, with at most 100,000 decoded values (including table keys/values). Net.Deserialize(data, value_limit) also accepts an optional value budget for direct callers. Partial transfers expire after 30 seconds, checked every five seconds; duplicate fragments do not extend this lifetime. The existing 100 packets/s client limit remains. These caps do not limit server-to-client route packs. Custom callers uploading larger data need to split it into separate messages. Invalid payloads are never passed to a registered callback.

Engine references: NavMesh area list, skin count, bounded decompression. Manual-spawn integration also follows the installed Sandbox gamemode/player.lua and commands.lua.

docs.title: Verification and remaining limits
docs.text:
python tools/test_core_audit.py runs isolated copies of the real modules through LuaJIT/lupa; the assertions live in lua/background_npcs_core/tests/sv_engineering_audit.lua. --baseline runs those checks against the starting dev source without changing the working tree. The same Lua file is available through SERVER bgn_selftest; it creates no live game entities. The offline harness isolates the actual spawn factory from unrelated GLua continue helpers; GLua syntax is checked separately with glualint dump-ast. For the object scan, unused continue paths are translated for LuaJIT; the checked valid-object and callback-removal paths run unchanged. See testing for the other checks.

The final offline run passed all 15 audit cases, the existing regression, actor LOD/debug, animator, carry, scenic, police-force and gang-skin checks, and seven build tests. The existing regression fixtures were updated for current witness/confirmed-damage, selected-enemy and actor-retirement contracts; production checks were not weakened to satisfy old fixtures. The complete current core and changed Tool passed GLua parsing, documentation passed strict EN/RU MkDocs build, and git diff --check passed.

No native game session was running for this audit. Multiplayer permissions/replication, actual NPC/NextBot movement and collision, door/vehicle physics and optional-addon combinations still need native verification. Script reload recreates class definitions while existing objects can retain old metatables and runtime references; updating every active action safely is outside these local fixes. Use a map restart for a clean body/brain validation. Externally changing GOAP action objects directly still requires GOAP.ClearCache().

The audit does not replace existing state machines, remove features, alter default ConVar values or rewrite users' route/configuration files. The new player-owner argument is optional; existing server spawn calls keep their behavior. No game saves, generated site files or Legacy sources are part of the changes.

docs.title: Independent recheck after d774aeb4
docs.text:
The two audit commits were checked against cde2f701, including their callers and test fixtures. The mechanics/UID/client-retirement fixes, recurring loops, random navigation, GOAP lower bound/cache, spawn permission and appearance changes, config IO, serialization bounds, seat receiver and language argument fixes remain justified. Table.Shuffle already copies its input; ResetStorage resets exactly the same five registries. Neither removal needs reverting. NPC/NextBot adapters and FSM/GOAP boundaries remain unchanged. Legacy still contains the constant-first regeneration expressions; its code is a reference, not evidence of correctness under the current seated-character contract.

The previous lifetime verification was incomplete. A living seated Actor can have a NULL engine body. Regeneration, ambient voices and foreign NPC disposition polling still assumed otherwise. The object scan also replaced a necessary IsValid check after yielding with IsAlive, introducing a regression. These services now validate the body before engine access; the scan also validates it after budget yields. The actor is retained for the existing vehicle recovery path. Four isolated tests cover these boundaries, service continuation and return to normal operation; the three coroutine cases failed before correction. Earlier mocks often made IsAlive track entity validity, masking this distinction.

Performance conclusions are limited: removing per-entity disk reads and duplicate copies removes work; replacing two yields per candidate reduces scan latency, not necessarily CPU time per second. More frequent completed scans can increase throughput and CPU usage. The shared budget remains cooperative. The admissible GOAP heuristic corrects plan cost ordering but can explore more states within the unchanged 200-state cap. The scheduler snapshot trades one small allocation per tick for safe iteration; it was a correctness fix. No native frame-time improvement is established by these tests.

Recheck validation: 21 audit cases, existing regression/LOD/debug/animation/carry/scenic/police/gang tests, seven build tests, full current-core GLua parsing, strict bilingual documentation build and diff checks. A running game was unavailable; native physics, multiplayer and optional-addon combinations remain unverified.

docs.title: Reduce load
docs.text: Run bgn_crowd_density low in the client console: a limit of 25 actors and no ghosts (an admin sets the server limit; any other player changes only their own ghosts, and only while the server does not run the ghost crowd). Restore the medium preset with bgn_crowd_density medium (35 actors, 40 ghosts). Type limits follow the total; existing actors need not disappear immediately.

docs.title: Russian interface, English voices
docs.text:
bgn_cl_ui_language russian
bgn_cl_voice_language english
bgn_cl_voices 1

Run in the client console. Set both language options to auto to follow the game language. The server's bgn_module_replics_language overrides phrase language for everyone when it is not auto.

docs.title: Citizens with one model and simple behaviour
docs.text:
Create a separate addon using the module guide, then add this file:

-- lua/background_npcs_core/custom_modules/config/sh_mytown_citizens.lua
local citizen = bgNPC.cfg.actors['citizen']
citizen.health = 80
citizen.default_models = false
citizen.models = { 'models/Humans/Group01/male_07.mdl' }
citizen.at_random = { walk = 80, idle = 20 }

These assignments replace whole tables. EditActor uses table.Merge, which can retain old keys and list entries. Reload the map after config changes; restart the game when adding a new addon directory.

docs.title: Two armed guards
docs.text:
-- lua/background_npcs_core/custom_modules/config/sh_mytown_guard.lua
bgNPC.cfg:SetActor('mytown_guard', {
    enabled = true,
    class = 'npc_citizen',
    name = 'Town guard',
    limit = 2,
    team = { 'residents' },
    health = 100,
    weapons = { 'weapon_pistol' },
    getting_weapon_chance = false,
    at_random = { walk = 70, idle = 30 },
    at_damage = { defense = 100 },
    at_protect = { defense = 100 },
})

class is required by SetActor. This independent configuration uses a fixed limit; do not add fullness, which takes priority over it. Reaction values are relative weights, not a guarantee of winning a fight.

docs.title: Find an actor and change its name
docs.text:
Put this in server-side custom_modules/postload/sv_mytown_inspect.lua. Only admins or the server console can run it:

concommand.Add('mytown_inspect', function(ply)
    if IsValid(ply) and not ply:IsAdmin() then return end
    local actor = bgNPC.Actors.GetFirst()
    if not actor or not actor:IsValid() then
        print('No actors spawned yet')
        return
    end
    local npc = actor:GetNPC()
    if not IsValid(npc) then return end
    actor:SetName('Town resident')
    print(actor:GetType(), npc:GetPos())
end)

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Subscribe to Background NPCs on Steam Workshop, or put this repository in garrysmod/addons/background-citizens. Avoid installing two copies.
  2. Start a map, for example gm_construct. Version 2.0 does not require SLibrary.
  3. Open the developer console and run bgn_menu. You can also use the Background NPCs icon in the C menu.
  4. On first launch follow the setup wizard. Its body step chooses engine NPCs with FSM like the old versions (NPC replacers and mods for standard NPCs keep working) or NextBots with GOAP and the ghost crowd. You can change everything later in the settings.
  5. Walk around and allow time for spawning. Actors generally appear outside your view; the limit is not an immediate spawn command.

Server settings require admin rights. Voice and interface choices are local to each player.

docs.title: Reopen setup
docs.text:
bgn_wizard

bgn_wizard all includes advanced steps. Changes in the wizard apply immediately; closing it does not undo them.

docs.title: Back to the old behavior
docs.text:
An admin can force the old-version setup (NPC body, FSM brain, no ghost crowd, no scenic NPCs) at any time:

bgn_classic
!bgn_classic

The first is a console command, the second is typed in chat (!bgnclassic and the / prefix work too). Admins only. The server part applies to the server, the client part only to the caller; NPCs already on the map keep their body, reload the map for a clean start. Admins also get this tip in chat when they join.

docs.title: Vehicles are optional
docs.text: Install Decent Vehicle, vehicle models referenced by your actor configuration, and suitable DV waypoints for the map. Pedestrian routes and DV waypoints are separate.

docs.title: Check navigation
docs.text: Run bgn_nav_info in the server console (or as an admin). The addon can use custom routes, a NavMesh or an HL2 nodegraph. See navigation before generating new routes; engine nav_generate is not required by the addon.

docs.title: Version history and documentation baseline
docs.text:
Version 2.6.0 (version.txt and bgNPC.VERSION; publication not verified) includes every change after tag 2.5.1 (a7f2d9da) through 463d21ca. The entries below labelled "Local 2.5.1" belong to 2.6.0. It also adds the optional cover-trace skip for spawn points (bgn_spawn_no_visibility_trace, default 0), medics revive only actors innocent toward residents, and bandits are no longer gang allies. See settings.

Local 2.5.1 dialogue fix (publication not verified): random state phrases and ambient coughs no longer interrupt conversation participants, including gathering and player-interruption phases. See conversations.

Local 2.5.1 follow-up fix (publication not verified): vehicle exits and lethal damage tolerate an already removed DV occupant entity; wanted detection skips living actors without a valid current entity. Stored character identity/health and normal exit obstruction checks are preserved. See vehicles and regressions.

Local 2.5.1 engineering audit (publication not verified): corrected disabled mechanics, recurring services, scheduler mutation, reload identity/snapshot counters, empty/sparse navigation queries, GOAP planning, appearance selection, regeneration and client receivers. Removed per-entity spawnmenu config IO; player-owned spawns now use gamemode permission/counting hooks. Network uploads have explicit bounds. Architecture and defaults remain; see the audit and verification limits.

Local 2.5.1 change (publication not verified): optional panic and threat search (bgn_threat_search, default off). An ally who sees a kill but not the killer (a trace from the victim, no view cone) panics (residents) or searches where the killer stood (police, gangs), walking within 1000 units of the killer; the spawner does not recycle them meanwhile. Anyone holding the killer's weapon class seen 3 checks in a row within 500 units in view becomes an enemy. See brains.

Local 2.5.1 team protection change (publication not verified): the vehicle offender exception (bgNPC.OffenderFromRamming, systems/sv_offender.lua) is removed. Running over a civilian or ramming police no longer moves a civilian driver from residents to offenders; police in a car ignore a civilian driver's ram. See wanted.

Local 2.5.1 SERVER optimization (publication not verified): the object scan behind BGN_ActorVisibleAtObject/BGN_ActorLookAtObject searches 100 units around an actor instead of 1000 (the built-in listeners react within 80 units), and its forward trace runs once per scan. The once-per-second foreign-hostility check rejects non-NPC entities first, and the static animation controller checks IsAlive only for animated actors. Behavior is unchanged.

Local 2.5.1 police-call fix (publication not verified): damage/protection reactions reject calls about already wanted or police-known enemies before enemy registration; entering a call also requires a valid selected enemy. Active-call completion rules are unchanged. See police calls.

Local 2.5.1 recycling change (publication not verified): spawn delay is 0 and the teleport limit is 10 per second. Move instead of removing remains enabled (1). The fast-check setting is removed: SERVER always uses one scheduler yield before each actor's recycling check. Saved values of the remaining cvars are preserved. See settings.

Local 2.5.1 citizen/police fix (publication not verified): friendly hits no longer start fear or confirmed conflict reactions; residents cannot be reported as wanted. Team changes reconcile targets/wanted/arrest. Only proven vehicle collisions can turn a civilian driver into an offender: running over a civilian or repeated police ramming, with a 3-second minimum and the existing 10% reaction chance. See wanted rules and behavior tree.

Local 2.5.1 audit fixes (publication not verified): NPC pursuit writes no longer extend the 60-second actor search; body replacement preserves position memory and target priority; police equipment follows the selected enemy. Negotiating officers cannot start/join sieges, payload ownership is resolved before damage reactions, and both NextBot unstuck teleport paths respect combat-radius protection. See the updated decision tree and developer checks.

Local 2.5.1 change (publication not verified): stable combat target priority, pursuit of last observed hidden positions, shared sighting memory, visible-only cover and combat recycling/unstuck protection (fixed 1000-unit radius). See brains.

Local 2.5.1 change (publication not verified): police radio lines for sieges (position, breach, grenade, manhack, outcome), a downed or lost target and hostage negotiation; sieges no longer mute actor voices; a wanted target is a known position even out of sight. See brains.

Local 2.5.1 change (publication not verified): GOAP single-exit room sieges with shared front/rear group positions, animation-gated metropolice manhacks/combine grenades and probabilistic door breaching/opening. The NavMesh-backed tactic and its limits are described in brains.

Local 2.5.1 change (publication not verified): optional held-lethal-weapon reaction for residents/police, default off, one-second LOS/FOV checks within 800 units. Weapon learning continues while off, excludes explosion/vehicle kills and persists new classes in a server cache/DATA file. See brains and the behavior tree.

Reviewed against Git through tag 2.3.0 (2258b49) and current 2.3.1 dev (7459c3c7, 2026-11-10). version.txt and bgNPC.VERSION both say 2.3.1. There are 48 commits between the tag and this baseline. A version string does not prove publication on Workshop.

Local Animator fixes after the baseline: dance starts after state cleanup, active donor animations synchronize to ready players entering PVS, stopping releases Animator-owned NPC freeze, and client copies preserve appearance at startup. See donor animations. Publication is not verified.

docs.title: Through 2.3.0
docs.text:
Period User-visible development and current documentation 1.x Original NPC/state system, route editor/compilation, configurable populations/teams, wanted/arrest, voices and optional addon integrations. Legacy routes and API compatibility remain relevant; old SLibrary/SNet examples are no longer the modern API. 2.0.0–2.0.1 Core rewrite with internal classes/network/scheduler, optional NextBot bodies and GOAP, navigation providers, settings UI, ghost crowd; fixes to ghost identity/entity lifetime. No required SLibrary. See architecture, brains, ghost crowd. 2.1.0–2.1.2 Behavior/settings expansion; first-start windows restricted to the single-player/listen-server owner; classic NPC body/FSM defaults restored and animation-death handling fixed. See quick start. 2.2.0 Classic spawnmenu pages and admin bgn_classic/chat aliases; corpse cleanup disabled by default so external cleanup can work. 2.2.1–2.2.2 Legacy route/duplication recovery and conversion; save/load ordering, preservation of existing and large graphs, cycle-safe actor saves, Workshop route export; arrested actors retain their pose. See navigation. 2.3.0 Offenders and visible teammate enemy sharing; NextBot unarmed animations/jump option/exit placement, movement/gesture/animation fixes; medics avoid a killed colleague's area; wanted after refusing arrest; police keep firearms through combat; dialogue voice/state sync and arrest ally protection.

Historical fixes describe the reason for current contracts, not separate APIs to reintroduce. The current body and brain defaults are npc and fsm.

docs.title: After 2.3.0: current 2.3.1 branch
docs.text:
Area Current behavior / owning documentation Spawn and debug Visibility checks and validation are atomic; admin actor overlay; unseen actor recycling, independent car radius; occluded whole-car spawning and pursuit-car catch-up; cover must block the sight line at least 40 units short of the spawn point, and the player's own car is not cover. Navigation, testing. Vehicles Measured simfphys headings, pedestrian detours, bounded recovery/alternate lanes, cleanup; native DV trace timing retained; police driver/passenger return and service-car access. Vehicles. Character lifecycle Stable actor/UID through DV entity replacement, safe health accessors, seat-specific exit hull checks and blocked-exit retention; seated damage goes through reaction/witness handling. Actor API. Policing Arrest module load order corrected, surrender no longer restarts a fight, officers hold arrest unless attacked; vehicle suspects are shot with ranged weapons; an actor standing still in a car gets the car break-in and arrest like a player (officers at the doors no longer block pulling it out); shots at any car base reach the occupants in full, and the police kill a driver after bgn_police_car_kill_time seconds; an unarmed actor out of a fight hit by the police gives up with 30%. Arrest. Gangs Black Raven/Red Wolf, light/heavy weapons/models, bounded initial rosters, rival wars, pack walking; direct victims still fight back outside roster caps. Gangs. Combat pacing Regional 60-second protection cooldown applies only between actors, not player/foreign NPC attacks, and never to the police; existing skirmish participation and self-defense remain. Officers in cars receive shared enemies and spot hostile NPCs/NextBots near the car, so they step out. Gangsters respawn after 30 seconds. Gangs. Medics and bodies Hopeless verdicts, body inspection/cleanup and completed-call release; vehicle collisions can be saved with normal chances; ambulance/medic protections. Medics and bodies. NextBots / damage Stuck recovery selects nearby free navigation space, avoids teleporting into vehicles; fixed custom-chair positioning. Brains, vehicles. GOAP Finished actions (cover, backup) advance the plan instead of being blocked; no endless cover loop; an officer holding an arrest makes the plan wait; picking a reaction never starts a surrender. GOAP plans only a fight the FSM started (defense/retreat); reactions are the config roll again, an enemy alone no longer starts a fight. An outnumbered officer takes cover, then calls backup, which makes its enemies wanted; one armed enemy no longer triggers backup. Brains. Wanted As in 1.x, the timer stays full while residents see the target, an actor too (not only while it fights); a target in a car is seen through its car body. A wanted NPC gains a level every bgn_wanted_level_up_period seconds. A wanted NPC is dropped after 15 s outside every player's field of view or farther than half of bgn_spawn_radius_visibility (obstacles ignored); the vehicle spawn exclusion moved to bgn_vehicle_spawn_visibility_radius. Wanted, menu. Lifecycle cleanup Actor bodies without a live registered actor are removed after 3 s regardless of health (frozen bodies killed while dormant), also with bgn_enable 0. Brains.

Working-tree fix after this baseline (version string 2.4.0, publication not verified): door scenes use fully closed doors, knocking faces the panel, and opening/removing the linked door returns participants to normal AI. The admin spawn command also uses the door finder. See scenic scenes. Five context-dependent scenes (both couches, radio operator, sky watch and door brace) were initially made manual-only; all scenic actors keep ordinary spawn/model-hook selection rather than overriding their models. GOAP actors in a hopeless fight can close and hold an open rotating door; police can kick it open, throwing the holder into a temporary ragdoll without extra damage. Recovery preserves the original actor/entity and health, requires free standing space, and restores its previous fight/flee behavior. See brains. The admin Scene debugger Tool adds visible manual placement, model/state/animation inspection, owned cleanup/Undo and a one-cycle GOAP door check. The console scene spawner shares its placement/Undo path. Chair reservations are released when scenic bodies are removed; previous seating states finish before scene placement. See scenic debugging. Scene debugger errors distinguish a missed door from an open/moving door or blocked floor space. Owned test actors are excluded from automatic population recycling/removal and scenic lifetime/distance cleanup. The scenic overhaul returns couches/radio to automatic indoor-only placement, removes cowering, splits wall fatigue from floor poses, adds ledge seating and solitary pose variants, and makes couch pairs atomic. Per-scene switches and per-actor carry_items settings control future spawning. Citizens have a combined 5% carried-item chance. A follow-up confines two-handed ration/newspaper poses to NextBots and visual ghosts; HL2 NPCs keep ordinary locomotion with only a clientside briefcase on their right-hand bone. The stock newspaper replaces a hidden driving parcel and follows both hands; no extracted or new game assets are shipped. Small items can be stowed. Briefcases on both body types stay attached until a combat state, never drop as physical objects, and need no luggage sequences. The admin carried-item debugger can force an item onto a calm unarmed actor.

Direct attackers without a shared team are now added as enemies on the first hit, including during an existing fight. Police no longer use door holding; door breaching remains available.

Prop-chair seating now finishes the close approach below the route completion distance. Seated scenic NextBots no longer rise or drift under physics; ledge placement additionally checks direct pelvis support.

Ghost carried items were removed in both modes; server-ghost materialization suppresses automatic carry selection. The briefcase hangs upright from the finger grip; the newspaper follows the fingertips at its lower edge, has upright text and leans away from the face by 15 degrees. Render bounds include hand positions so close-up views do not cull the props.

The entity-cache warm-up on first player spawn was restored: BGN temporarily spawns configured NPCs and vehicles to warm their resources. NextBot relationships now use the most frequent disposition of each foreign NPC towards server players, with neutral ties, instead of hidden NPC probes. Ordinary HL2 NPC body relationships retain their existing rules. See brains.

Local gang behavior change after the baseline above: walking packs of up to three; the capped random fight roster is replaced by support for all visible same-gang allies, including late arrivals. bgn_gang_help_chance is no longer used; bgn_enemy_share_period controls the support interval. See gangs.

Local debug UI addition: Spawnmenu Options now has a Debugging page with separate overlays, an admin-only server actor inspector (recent states/reactions, weights and cached GOAP plan/facts), LOS/FOV visualization and an actor camera with automatic release. See debug controls. The native follow-up enlarges/scales debug text, wraps inspector lines and preserves the camera when the actor list is refreshed; overlay, visibility, path, damage, GOAP and camera checks were exercised in single-player. Visual verification also fixed the NextBot camera falling to its feet (server-only eye method) and the viewed head clipping into the camera; server eye frames and temporary body rendering suppression fix both.

Local debug redesign: editor/debug Tools now have separate categories. UID-based inspection defaults to one actor and records actual perception and team handoffs, with bounded history, configurable HUD/3D2D, distances, WH, filters and freeze. Cached line meshes replace the separate immediate world passes. Scene previews and hand markers share these controls; actor movement restores prior control flags/state. Gameplay stealth rules are unchanged. Native debugging also exposed and fixed carried-model culling after actor teleportation. See debug controls.

A 2026-11-12 audit of the current branch against 1.13.7 (what stayed, what changed, what can break old behavior) is in comparison with 1.13.

docs.title: Reproduce the comparison
docs.text:
git log --reverse --no-merges --oneline 2.3.0
git log --reverse --oneline 2.3.0..7459c3c7
git diff --stat 2.3.0 7459c3c7 -- lua docs

Read implementation and callers before changing a documented contract. Commit subjects alone do not prove behavior. Maintenance rules.

Local change: distant actor logic uses configurable staggered pause/active windows; see LOD.

Local weapon change: NextBot pistol single/short bursts, witness-local police harm limits, lifecycle cleanup and armed arrest aim. See brains.

Local network change: actor PVS sync sends identity (entity, type, generation, class, model, name, gender) only on first sight or rebind and otherwise only the changed state part; sends are capped at 8 per tick. See architecture.

Local vehicle fix: forced ejection during car seizure now uses the original passengers rather than deep copies of their actors. Restored bodies keep their registered identity and AI instead of freezing and later being removed as orphans. See vehicles.

Local vehicle fix 2: an actor leaving a moving car (police arriving at a chase) is immune to damage from that same car for 3 seconds, so a fast car no longer kills the officer on exit, after which the lifeless body stood still and was removed. See vehicles.

Local 2.5.1 working-tree change (publication not verified): confirmed-damage conflict memory, attacker-only witnesses, caller-visible help, shared player/actor wanted thresholds, foreign hostility wanted and primary-officer arrest escalation. See wanted and arrest.

Local follow-up: attacking an observer's known enemy does not incriminate a non-hostile attacker; existing enemy lists and bidirectional D_HT forbid the exception. It applies before initiator selection, also to arrest initiation/non-police harm counts. The observer's own enemies now count in IsEnemyOfTeam. See conflicts.

Local follow-up: an active police phone call no longer requires continuous LOS or stops because the target became wanted/police. Threat interruption is strictly below 300 units. Allied help and GOAP replanning preserve the active call; entry limits and completion filters remain. See wanted.

docs.title: Comparison with 1.13 (Classic)
docs.text:
Audit date: 2026-11-12. Compared: the Classic release 1.13.7 (tag 1.13.7, SLibrary required) and the current branch dev at da58946d (version 2.4.0 in the working tree, publication on Workshop not verified). The comparison is static: source read side by side, whitespace ignored. It was not checked in game. Match percentages below count unchanged lines, not identical behavior.

1.13.7 Current Lua files in background_npcs_core 212 298 Lua lines (with compiled routes) ~20,500 ~36,000 Dependency SLibrary none Files in sound/materials/models/resource 47 981

Summary. The external contract (configuration, cvars, hooks, commands, saved data) is nearly unchanged. The internals were rewritten. With default settings the body is still an HL2 NPC (bgn_actor_body npc) and the brain is the FSM (bgn_brain fsm), but behavior in game differs because of new systems and changed spawn, navigation and wanted rules.

docs.title: Unchanged
docs.text:
• Configuration: config/sh_main.lua, sh_config.lua, sh_player.lua, custom_modules/* examples, DarkRP money and door modules are identical except for whitespace.
  • Extension points: custom_modules/config|preload|postload, bgNPC.cfg.*, bgNPC.cfg:SetActor/SetActorData, legacy config adapter (config/sh_oldconfig.lua).
  • Hooks: all 54 BGN_* hooks fired by 1.13 are still fired with the same arguments (only local variable names differ). Exception in meaning: see BGN_WantedLevelDown below.
  • Actor methods: all 116 old methods exist; StopStaticSequence is an alias of ResetSequence.
  • Global API: all 85 bgNPC:* methods exist, directly or through compatibility aliases in api/compat/sh_legacy.lua.
  • Commands: all old console commands remain except bgn_cl_draw_chunks_reload (chunk system removed) and cmd_bgn_spawnmenu_default_spawner (already commented out in 1.13).
  • Data: background_npcs/nodes/*.dat|json, citizens_points/, seats/, spawn_area/, custom.dat. Old route files are converted to the new graph on load and kept; see navigation. Bundled map compile files still write the 1.2 route format.
  • Tools and integrations: all old Tools, DV entities and ULX modules.

docs.title: Partly changed (same logic, rewritten code)
docs.text:
Area Unchanged lines FSM states walk, idle, fear, retreat, run_from_danger, steal, killer, impingement, dyspnea, chair seating, zombie 57–92% defense / arrest states 68% / 66% Spawner core / actor spawner / spawn zones / DV spawner 58% / 49% / 77% / 82% Wanted class / wanted actions (network message names kept, SNet replaced) 57% / 66% Relationships / team parent / damage and shot reactions 54% / 77% / 35–59% Spawnmenu, ambient sound 76–85%, 77%

Most of the difference is the replacement of SLibrary calls by bgNPC.*. Actor configs changed in content only in: citizens getting_weapon_chance 30 → 10 and carry_items; gang respawn_delay = 30; dialogue weights.

docs.title: Strongly changed
docs.text:
• Core: classes/, global/, actions/ replaced by a single actor update loop with LOD, body adapters (HL2 NPC / NextBot) and brains (FSM / GOAP); see architecture and brains.
  • Navigation: own nodes and the runtime "dynamic mesh" replaced by providers (bgn_nav_provider auto: saved route → navmesh → nodegraph → own generator). Removed cvars: bgn_dynamic_nodes_type, bgn_dynamic_nodes_alternative, bgn_enable_dynamic_nodes_only_when_mesh_not_exists, bgn_chunk_*.
  • Dialogues: bgNPC.cfg.dialogues (HL2 vo/* lines) replaced by bgNPC.cfg.conversations with own voices; see conversations.
  • Tactical groups: new implementation (column/wedge/line formations, leader, wounded in the rear), enabled by default. bgNPC:GetTacticalGroupGetFirstEnemy / GetTacticalGroupGetNearEnemy were removed without an alias.
  • Gangs: gangster is disabled; two gangs at 5% each with rival wars (bgn_gang_war_chance 0.5) and pack walking; see gangs.
  • New systems: medics and bodies (up to 4), scenic scenes (bgn_scenic 1, up to 4), carried items (5% of citizens), door hold/breach and temporary ragdoll, car break-in on arrest, offenders, actor fight cooldown, ghost crowd (off), weapon pickup (off).
  • UI: tool_options/* panels replaced by the settings window; old panels partly available through bgn_classic.

docs.title: Changed defaults
docs.text:
Cvar 1.13.7 Current bgn_spawn_radius_visibility 2500 2000 bgn_module_replics_language english auto bgn_module_tactical_groups 0 1

About 50 cvars were added. Removed cvars (bgn_chunk_*, dynamic node options above, bgn_optimize_no_think_*) no longer have any effect.

docs.title: Changes that can break 1.13 behavior
docs.text:
1. Recycling. 1.13 moved an actor only beyond bgn_spawn_radius, or beyond the visibility radius when unseen. Now any actor unseen by players for bgn_actor_unseen_time (30 s) can be moved, even close behind a wall (spawner/sv_actor_remover.lua).
  2. Maps without routes but with a navmesh. Runtime point generation is replaced by navmesh areas as points; HL2 NPCs walk to them with SCHED_FORCED_GO. Spawn and route distribution differ; on a map with a navmesh but no .ain nodegraph HL2 NPCs may walk poorly to far areas.
  3. State update rate. The old state machine called update almost every frame. Now the brain runs every 0.2 s near players and 1 s far away; distant unarmed actors alternate 2 s pause / 1 s active (1.13 froze them completely beyond 500 units). Third-party states registered with SetStateAction that rely on frequent update react more slowly.
  4. defense in classic mode: a civilian leaves the fight to the police (fear); a wanted actor retreats when the enemy is farther than 300 units and its health is under 50%; fighters may seize cars; with tactical groups the squad drives movement; self-healing no longer arms actors that have getting_weapon_chance.
  5. Wanted: a wanted NPC (not a player) is dropped after 15 s outside every player's view; its level rises every 60 s; medics and arrested targets cannot become wanted; LevelDown() at level 1 now removes the wanted status (1.13: no-op); the second argument of BGN_WantedLevelDown is now the level instead of the kill counter. The addon itself does not call LevelDown, only external addons are affected. See wanted.
  6. Custom dialogues in bgNPC.cfg.dialogues are silently ignored.
  7. Phrase language. 1.13 preferred the game language over the cvar; now the server bgn_module_replics_language overrides everything, so a server with a saved english value forces English on Russian players. The server picks phrase indexes from the English table, so a custom language file must have the same number of phrases. See voices.
  8. Population: two gangs and wars instead of gangster, plus medics, scenes and squads, change both the mix and the frequency of fights. Disabling gangster by type name now leaves the gangs active.
  9. Synthetic OnNPCKilled: actor/components/sh_vehicle.lua runs OnNPCKilled for an actor killed in a car; third-party kill or money counters can see an unexpected or extra event.

Internal hook.Add / net identifiers (about 60, e.g. BGN_ThinkProcess) disappeared; they are not a public contract.

docs.title: Running the 1.13 Classic core
docs.text:
The Classic core (1.13.7) ships inside this addon in lua/background_npcs_legacy/, with a trimmed copy of SLibrary (no separate SLibrary addon needed). Choose which core loads with the bgn_loader core|legacy command (autocomplete, superadmin or server console). The choice is stored in data/background_npcs/loader.txt; the server publishes it to clients through the internal replicated ConVar bgn_loader_active:

Value Loads core (default) background_npcs_core (current) legacy background_npcs_legacy (Classic 1.13.7)

Run bgn_loader legacy and restart the map; changing it at runtime does nothing until then. Both cores share the bgn_* settings, route files and compiled map data. Classic uses its own entities (bgn_legacy_dv_police, bgn_legacy_dv_passenger) and tools (bgn_legacy_*); the tools of the inactive core are hidden from the tool menu. Not carried over: the Classic poll and update-check pages. Tested: both loaders start on gm_construct without Lua errors and spawn actors; Classic gameplay was not played through.

docs.title: Limits of this audit
docs.text: Not checked: behavior in game; semantic equivalence of each compatibility alias beyond its name; DV and DarkRP modules beyond file level. Highest risks: item 1 (recycling) and item 2 (navigation source).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check No actors Open bgn_menu, enable actor types and give them nonzero limits. Walk around and run bgn_nav_info on the server. No navigation points Try bgn_nav_generate around 1500, then bgn_nav_info. This uses the addon's point generator. bgn_nav_generate covers the map; bgn_nav_generate stop cancels it. See navigation. Server settings missing or won't change They require admin rights and are hidden from ordinary players. Run bgn_test_settings: it shows what the server thinks of your group. Custom module not loading Check lua/background_npcs_core/custom_modules/config/, the sh_ prefix and Lua errors in the console. Restart after creating a new addon directory. Old models or reactions remain EditActor merges tables. Replace the field directly, as in the examples. No cars Check Decent Vehicle, installed models listed in vehicles, a nonzero max_vehicle and DV waypoints. Pedestrian points do not replace DV routes. No voices Check bgn_cl_voices 1, voice language and installed sound files. Both actor modes use the same conversation clips. Low FPS Start with bgn_crowd_density low. High ghost counts cost client FPS too; see ghost crowd.

When reporting a bug, run the testing mode (bgn_test) and attach the copied log. If that is not enough, include the map, gamemode, bgn_nav_info output, Lua errors and reproduction steps. Built-in checks: bgn_selftest on the server and bgn_selftest_cl on the client; these do not replace testing behaviour in game.

docs.title: Actor API
docs.text:
An actor is a stable character record associated with an engine entity. Bodies and brains exist on the server; the client receives presentation data.

  • Server methods: construction, state changes, movement, combat, vehicles, speech and removal.
  • Client methods: state snapshots and settings UI.
  • Shared methods: identity, health, state/enemy/target queries and public namespaces.

Get an actor using bgNPC.Actors.Get(entity), GetByUid(uid) or GetFirst(). A lookup may return nil. Validate actor:GetNPC() with IsValid.

Use bgNPC.Actor.Create(npc, actor_type) on the server to bind a new entity. BGN_ACTOR:Instance remains a compatibility alias. Do not register an entity twice.

Boarding a DV vehicle keeps the actor and UID, replaces the entity with a DV visual and recreates the saved NPC/NextBot on exit. Fetch the entity again after BGN_ActorEntityChanged(actor, old, new); addon-private entity state needs its own integration. Use Health() / GetMaxHealth() instead of assuming the visual has NPC methods.

Client snapshots are sent on a 0.25-second service cycle to ready players in PVS when data changes. They contain identity, entity generation, state name/group, enemies/targets and animation flags; server body/brain, full state data and configuration mutations are not mirrored in full.

See examples and architecture.

docs.title: Instance
docs.text:
SERVER, legacy compatibility alias. Prefer:

local actor = bgNPC.Actor.Create(npc, 'citizen')
if not actor then return end

Equivalent compatibility call: BGN_ACTOR:Instance(npc, npc_type, custom_uid, not_sync_actor_on_client, not_auto_added_to_list).

npc is a valid entity, npc_type is an actor configuration ID. Optional custom_uid supplies an identity; the two optional booleans suppress initial client sync and automatic registration. Leave them unset for normal addons. Returns an actor or nil for invalid input; do not bind an already registered entity.

Implementation: actor/sh_actor.lua, Actor.Create / Actor:Init. Server API.

docs.title: AddEnemy
docs.text:
Realm: SERVER (supported usage).

actor:AddEnemy(ent, reaction, always_visible)

Adds an entity enemy with optional reaction and always_visible flag; hooks, team rules may reject it.

Source: lua/background_npcs_core/actor/components/sh_enemies.lua.

Realm reference.

docs.title: AddTarget
docs.text:
Realm: SERVER (supported usage).

actor:AddTarget(ent)

Adds a valid entity target unless already present; requires targets_controller.

Source: lua/background_npcs_core/actor/components/sh_targets.lua.

Realm reference.

docs.title: CallForHelp
docs.text:
Realm: SERVER (supported usage).

actor:CallForHelp(enemy)

Asks living teammates within 1000 units who have LOS to the caller to react to the enemy. Seeing the enemy is not required; FOV is not checked. The enemy must not share a team with either the caller or the recipient; this check runs before changing the recipient’s state. The caller needs call_for_help, a valid enemy and positive health. BGN_PreCallForHelp can cancel; arrest protection, enemy restrictions and protection cooldown still apply.

Source: lua/background_npcs_core/actor/components/sh_combat.lua.

Realm reference.

docs.title: CallStateAction
docs.text:
Realm: SERVER (supported usage).

actor:CallStateAction(state_name, func_name, ...)

Calls a registered callback with this actor and extra arguments; nil state_name uses the current state.

Source: lua/background_npcs_core/actor/components/sh_state.lua.

Realm reference.

docs.title: ClearSchedule
docs.text:
Realm: SERVER (supported usage).

docs.title: EnemiesRecalculate
docs.text:
Realm: SERVER (supported usage).

actor:EnemiesRecalculate()

Updates counts, observes all visible known enemies, drops dead/forgotten enemies and assigns GetEnemy() to the body; requires a valid body. Ordinary hidden enemies expire after more than 60 seconds from their observation/report timestamp. Engine pursuit-memory writes do not renew this timestamp. Wanted and always-visible exceptions remain. See combat memory.

docs.title: EnterVehicle
docs.text:
Server: actor:EnterVehicle(vehicle, animate) requests boarding after a 0.5-second delay and returns the delay. With animate (used by go_to_police_car) the actor stops and turns to the car (no sit animation; the state go_to_police_car first walks it to within about 70 units of the car's hull) before disappearing; it does not board if it was moved more than 300 units from the car meanwhile. It requires DV, use_vehicle, a valid vehicle and an available allowed seat. Permission and availability are checked again when boarding; there is no synchronous success result.

Boarding preserves the actor object and UID, stores its body and equipment, removes the physical NPC/NextBot and binds the actor to the DV driver/passenger entity. BGN_OnEnterVehicle(actor, provider) fires after success. Only police actors may board designated police vehicles.

docs.title: ExitVehicle
docs.text:
Server: actor:ExitVehicle(forced) returns true after recreating and rebinding the original body, or false if it cannot exit. forced bypasses the police dismount policy, but still requires a valid vehicle and a safe position.

Position selection tries the nearest configured model exit, then positions beside the actor's seat and the opposite side. Ground, height, body clearance and overlap with standing actors are checked. If no spot is free, the actor stays aboard. Appearance, health, equipment and actor identity are preserved; BGN_OnExitVehicle(actor, provider) fires after success.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Returns the entity currently associated with the actor: an NPC/NextBot on foot or a DV driver/passenger anim entity while seated. Can return "NULL". Boarding removes the old body and exiting recreates it; fetch this value again after either transition. The actor object and UID remain stable.

docs.title: Return
docs.text: 1. Entity - entity associated with an actor, or NULL

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Paint the NPC.

    local npc_color = Color(10, 52, 255)
    local actor = bgNPC.Actors.GetFirst()
    if not actor or not actor:IsValid() then return end
    local npc = actor:GetNPC()
    if not IsValid(npc) then return end
    npc:SetColor(npc_color)

        print(actor:GetName(), data.state, data.time)

end

Source: lua/background_npcs_core/ui/menu/cl_menu.lua. See menu extensions for a complete page example.

API Purpose bgNPC.Menu.AddPage(id, def) Register {title, order, icon, group, build}; build receives a page. bgNPC.Menu.RemovePage(id) Remove a registered page. bgNPC.Menu.Open(page_id), Close(), IsOpen() Window lifecycle. bgNPC.Menu.ShowPage(page_id) Select an existing page. bgNPC.Menu.Text(value), Phrase(key) Resolve localized display text. bgNPC.Menu.IsAdmin() UI visibility check; server permission checks remain authoritative. bgNPC.Actors.ReceiveBinding(npc, npc_type, uid, info, generation, class, model) Internal receiver: ignores stale generations and rebinds the existing UID. docs.text:
Run gameplay changes on SERVER. Many methods are declared in sh_ files for compatibility but depend on a server body, brain, provider or gameplay module.

bgNPC.Actor.New(...) is the unchecked class constructor; extensions should use bgNPC.Actor.Create(...). actor:StopStaticSequence() is an alias of ResetSequence().

docs.text: bgNPC.Combat.ResolveVehicleAttacker(attacker, inflictor) resolves a valid siege payload owner from the attacker, falling back to the optional inflictor, then resolves a driven vehicle to its driver. Without a valid owner or vehicle conversion it returns the supplied attacker; an engine IsVehicle() entity without a valid driver returns nil. Existing one-argument calls remain valid. Damage handlers pass both entities before team/protection checks. Source: api/sv_combat.lua.

docs.title: Namespaces and services
docs.text:
API Contract / source bgNPC:SpawnActor(npc_type, desiredPosition, enableSpawnEffect, require_hidden, owner) Creates an actor; owner is optional. When supplied, requires a valid living player (or admin), lets PlayerSpawnNPC veto the resolved NPC class before creation, sets creator and emits PlayerSpawnedNPC for gamemode counting. Menu/Tool pass their player; automatic population omits it. Check the result before use. Source: spawner/sv_spawner.lua. bgNPC.Statistics.AddKill(attacker, actor) Adds and synchronizes a kill count. bgNPC.Statistics.Reset(attacker), ResetAll() Clears and synchronizes statistics. bgNPC.Actors.Rebind(actor, npc) Internal body replacement; updates registries/references and emits BGN_ActorEntityChanged. Use the normal vehicle lifecycle instead of calling directly. bgNPC.Combat Weapon skill/equipment, fighting checks, resolving vehicle attackers and enemies: api/sv_combat.lua. bgNPC.Nav Provider selection, loading and pathfinding: nav/sv_nav.lua; see navigation. bgNPC.GOAP Planner actions/sensors: see brains. bgNPC.Tasks Cooperative work with yield/wait/budget; core/sh_tasks.lua. Each realm has its own scheduler.

bgNPC.Combat.CanPoliceUseStunstick(officer, suspect) returns the SERVER baton eligibility from wanted status, kill evidence, that officer's witnessed harm and whether any of the officer's enemies has hit someone from farther than 500 units. bgNPC.Combat.ResetPoliceThreat(suspect) clears kill evidence/counters and officer harm records; use only for a completed reset, not initial wanted escalation. BGN_PostVehicleDamage(actor, attacker, amount) fires on SERVER after virtual seated health is updated, before death handling.

bgNPC.Combat.CanWitness(actor, attacker, check_view) checks a living observer, a valid attacker, distance up to 2500 and LOS to the attacker; actor attackers also require FOV. check_view = true requires FOV for any attacker. It returns a visibility boolean and may return the LOS hit entity as its second value. BGN_ConfirmedDamage(attacker, target, amount) fires on SERVER after positive actual damage, including seated health, after recording the initiator and evaluating existing-arrest harm limits; initial arrest and witnesses run from this notification. Consensual brawls and ignored attackers are excluded; friend mode keeps its existing player-side reaction override instead of dispatching this notification for player conflicts. BGN_PostReactionTakeDamage remains a pre-application reaction hook and does not prove actual damage. See conflicts.

bgNPC.Combat.IsAttackingEnemy(actor, target, attacker) returns a SERVER boolean: the target is already that observer's enemy, while observer and attacker have no enemy-list hostility or D_HT in either direction. It reads configured actor relationships, body dispositions (including NextBots) and available entity Disposition methods. Invalid entities and direct hits on the observer return false; missing optional methods do not imply hatred. ResolveEnemy returns nil for this exception before selection by initiator, team or wanted status; the observer stays out of that hit. The predicate does not change teams, enemy lists or conflict memory.

docs.title: Data contracts
docs.text:
• Points.GetRandom returns a Vector or nil; an empty graph radius query stays empty instead of selecting elsewhere. NavMesh sampling uses actual areas. On CLIENT this API returns nil.
  • Actors.Get, GetByUid, GetFirst and nearest lookups can return nil. GetAll, type lists and NPC lists expose internal storage: do not mutate them.
  • Config.GetActor returns a cached resolved table or nil: copy before editing. After changing bgNPC.cfg.actors, call Config.ClearCache; existing actors keep their own copies.
  • States.Register(name, group, callbacks) registers behavior callbacks in each realm where executed. Execute AI callbacks on the server.
  • Points wraps the active navigation provider. Its useful graph/path data is server-side; use the navigation editor's synchronization for client route editing.
  • Statistics.Get returns a count for a type, or a table without a type; GetSum returns the total. Client data arrives via network events.
  • Modules.Get(name) may return nil; availability depends on realm and load stage. A shared accessor does not make a server module available on the client.

docs.title: Arrest
docs.text:
SERVER rejects arrest registration for a teammate of the primary officer. Changing a suspect's team to match that officer removes its existing arrest; friendly damage does not reach confirmed-harm escalation.

Code: lua/background_npcs_core/systems/arrest/, the police state brain/fsm/states/sv_arrest.lua. Settings window: Arrest.

Cvar (server) Default Meaning bgn_arrest_mode 1 the police try to arrest first bgn_arrest_time 5 seconds the detention takes bgn_arrest_time_limit 20 seconds to give up; then the police shoot bgn_arrest_surrender_delay 10 the second chance (below); 0 off bgn_arrest_car_wait 6 car break-in: seconds standing still in a car with the police at it; 0 off bgn_arrest_car_time 8 car break-in: seconds it takes, then the arrest bgn_police_car_kill_time 30 an actor in a car: seconds from the first police hit, then their next hit kills; 0 off bgn_arrest_safe_weapons mlp_hoof,empty,weapon_card,... comma-separated weapon classes that don't count as being armed

A player gives up by looking at the ground (pitch over 40°) near the officer. NPC targets give up by the arrest_surrender state: an actor (an NPC or a NextBot body, e.g. a gangster) that attacks near the police may give up, 5% on its first attack and 10% on each later one, only while below half its maximum health. An actor on foot hit by an officer while it holds no active weapon and is not fighting (defense, killer, zombie, take_cover, pick_up_weapon, brawl) gives up with 30% per hit, only when that officer has it as an enemy: a stray police bullet never arrests a bystander (systems/arrest/sv_surrender.lua). Players and actors share the refusal time limit and the escalation rules below. An attacked officer may defend itself.

A surrender never turns back into a fight: when the arrest ends or times out, the actor stops regarding the officers as enemies. If every officer within 2500 units is busy with another target (none arrests or hunts it), it slips away (retreat); otherwise it just calms down.

docs.title: Police weapon choice and witnessed harm
docs.text:
SERVER allows a stunstick only against a non-wanted suspect with no recorded kills, no witnessed allied victim left at or below 30% health, and at most five distinct witnessed allied victims. A sixth victim forbids the baton. Any enemy of the officer that has hit anyone (player or NPC) from farther than 500 units also forbids it, until that enemy's threat is reset. A gun in the suspect's hands alone does not forbid it. A vehicle still requires a ranged weapon. Metropolice otherwise use their assigned main weapon (pistol fallback); other police classes keep their main-weapon rules. Weapon choice is re-evaluated instead of being latched for the whole state.

api/sv_police_force.lua stores each officer's private police_harm[suspect] = {victims, count, critical}. Only actual damage counts, once per allied actor UID; the officer must see the attacker with gameplay LOS within 2500 HU (also FOV for an attacking actor), or be the victim. Wanted status does not bypass this observation. Seated actors feed the same logic after virtual health damage. Serious injury remains remembered even if that ally later heals. No global per-frame victim scan is performed.

Death (including silent player death), removal, completed arrest and normal wanted removal clear the suspect's kill evidence and all officers' corresponding harm records. Body replacement transfers records instead of counting another suspect. Bulk wanted clearing and dead-target cleanup use normal removal events. Kill counters also reset on initial wanted escalation in the existing wanted system; the separate kill flag survives that counter reset so the first kill still forbids a baton. BGN_PlayerArrest handlers can inspect pre-reset statistics; completed-arrest cleanup follows the hook even when an integration handles the default outcome.

During an arrest, police keep the chosen weapon. Wanted suspects, killers and serious/multiple-victim offenders stay under the main weapon; a protected surrender clears the combat enemy and holds aim without granting permission to fire. This does not change arrest eligibility or the protection against damage from law allies.

Refusal or an escalation condition below ends the arrest and makes a player or actor wanted if bgn_enable_wanted_mode is enabled. An existing wanted record is neither reset nor extended. Disabling arrest mode does not count as a refusal.

docs.title: Car break-in
docs.text:
systems/arrest/sv_car_breakin.lua: a suspect (a player, or an actor that is not an officer) who stands still in a vehicle (rolling up to 64 units counts as standing) for bgn_arrest_car_wait seconds while the police are after them (fighting or arresting, within 2000 units). The officers then hold fire, get out of their cars and run to it (state police_car_breakin: their enemies are put aside and come back when it stops). Once one is within 300 units the break-in starts (police_seize line) and takes bgn_arrest_car_time seconds: a player sees a bar shrinking from both sides to the middle (cl_car_breakin.lua, blinking in the last quarter). Driving 64 units away cancels it and the officers fight again. The officers can't be pulled away by anything else (not_stop; only forced states such as an arrest); an officer stepping away from the car only pauses the bar, it never starts over.
