At the end the player is pulled out and arrested like at the end of an arrest (BGN_PlayerArrest, or the fade and KillSilent). An actor is pulled out of the car (the officers at the doors do not block the exit, only the world and props do; a blocked exit retries on the next tick) and gives up to the officer at the car (ArrestModule:Surrender): it goes to arrest_surrender, the officer to arrest, and the usual arrest finishes it. The progress is kept on the suspect's entity (ent.bgn_still); ArrestModule:BreakinCar(ent) returns the car of a called break-in.

A shot at a car managed by the addon (any base: a prop_vehicle_jeep or a scripted simfphys/LVS/Glide chassis) hits every occupant for the full damage; a crash (DMG_CRUSH, DMG_VEHICLE) only for 1/2-1/10 of it (modules/dv/sv_car_damage_reaction.lua). When the police have not killed an actor in a car within bgn_police_car_kill_time seconds of their first hit on it, their next hit kills it (Actor:TakeVehicleDamage); 60 seconds without a police hit, or stepping out, start the time over.

docs.title: Second chance
docs.text:
systems/arrest/sv_surrender.lua: a player the police shoot at who carries only safe weapons (or nothing) and has hurt no one for bgn_arrest_surrender_delay seconds is offered an arrest again, even after a rampage or while wanted: every officer fighting the player switches to arrest (police_surrender voice line). Refusing within the time limit, or meeting the harm/escape conditions below, ends the chance. The next chance comes after time limit + delay. Hook: BGN_PlayerSurrenderChance(ply, police_actor).

Fist fights never lead to shooting: the police arrest both fighters (Conversations).

docs.title: Holding an arrest
docs.text: Players and actors use the same refusal deadline. One primary officer conducts the arrest; other officers in the arrest state remain ready without advancing detention. Officers hold the arrest unless attacked. Allied police damage to a protected active arrest target is suppressed; an attacked officer retains self-defense. Sources: systems/arrest/sv_arrest.lua, brain/fsm/states/sv_arrest.lua.

docs.title: Escalation during an arrest
docs.text:
SERVER starts an arrest after confirmed damage, so blocked/zero hits do not start one and the opening hit is not a subsequent violation. During that attempt, any of these ends arrest and requests wanted status:

  • Refusal after bgn_arrest_time_limit while not in detention (players and actors).
  • Damage to a police actor, or killing a player, NPC or actor.
  • Damage leaving a non-police actor below 30% of maximum health, unless that victim initiated its conflict with the suspect.
  • Damage to more than three distinct non-police actors that did not initiate their conflicts with the suspect. Repeated hits count once per actor UID, for this arrest attempt.
  • Leaving the primary officer's 250-unit zone after that officer first reached it. Until then, moving while the officer approaches is not escape. The last close officer position and suspect movement are checked too, so an officer moving away cannot alone trigger escape.

Compliance is checked every 0.25 seconds and during primary-officer updates, independently of AI state/LOD. Actual detention still needs a distance of 200 units and the surrender pose. Damage limits use confirmed post-damage health, including seated actors. Body replacement preserves the arrest attempt and its victim count. Exactly 30% and exactly three victims do not escalate. These limits are separate from the weapon-choice thresholds above. With wanted disabled, escalation still ends arrest; peaceful mode prevents wanted assignment. See conflict memory.

Damage to the primary officer's known enemy is excluded from the non-police victim count and the below-30% injury condition when the suspect and officer have no existing enemy relationship or D_HT in either direction. The same rule prevents initiating an arrest solely for attacking a common enemy. Hitting a police actor, killing during arrest, refusal and escape keep their separate escalation rules. The weapon-choice harm memory also excludes such common-enemy hits; range and kill evidence retain their existing meaning. See conflict rules.

docs.title: Arrest decision tree
docs.text:
This SERVER branch follows the damage and enemy-selection tree. It describes the local 2.5.1 working tree, not verified Workshop behavior.

Confirmed damage by a player/ACTOR
├─ Arrest mode off or the attacker already wanted → do not start a new arrest here
├─ No existing arrest record
│  ├─ Find an officer: the victim if police, otherwise within 700 of A, then V
│  ├─ Officer is not the victim → must witness the real attacker
│  ├─ ResolveEnemy returns none (including common enemy) → no arrest
│  ├─ Chosen side is foreign, neither player nor ACTOR → request enemy, no arrest
│  └─ Chosen side is player/ACTOR → create arrest record and assign primary officer
│     └─ An ACTOR must surrender to enter detention; otherwise the record can
│        persist while the officer defends, with compliance checked by the timer
└─ Existing arrest: harm was evaluated before BGN_ConfirmedDamage
   ├─ Damaged victim is a police ACTOR → escalate
   ├─ Victim is not an ACTOR → no injury/victim-count escalation
   ├─ Common-enemy exception for the primary officer → exclude this hit
   ├─ Victim initiated its conflict with the suspect → exclude this hit
   └─ Other non-police ACTOR → count each UID once
      └─ Count >3 or post-damage health <30% → escalate

Death callbacks: the suspect kills someone during an active arrest → escalate
(independent of the injury exemptions above)

Primary-officer compliance (timer every 0.25 s, plus state updates)
├─ Mode off / no active record → no escalation here
├─ No living primary officer found → wait for replacement; no compliance check
├─ Officer within 250 → refresh the last close officer position
├─ Officer has never been within 250 → no escape yet; deadline check still applies
├─ Both current and last-close officer distances >250, and suspect moved
│  └─ Escape → escalate
└─ Not detained and warning deadline expired → refusal → escalate

Escalate
├─ Mark this attempt non-arrestable and return the primary officer to defense
└─ Wanted enabled and not peaceful → request wanted (normal exclusions remain)

The warning deadline starts when the record is created; waiting for the officer to approach does not pause it. Escape and actual detention have different radii (250 and 200). Health/count exemptions do not excuse a police hit or an arrest-time kill. Weapon choice is a separate assessment, not another route to automatically assign an enemy. Successful detention, body replacement and second-chance behavior follow the sections above.

docs.title: Actor brains
docs.text: An actor is split into an actor (data and rules), a body (actor.body: everything that talks to the engine entity: movement, schedules, relationships, weapons, animation) and a brain (actor.brain: decisions). Bodies and brains exist on the server only.

docs.title: Pursuing an occluded target
docs.text:
SERVER keeps a stable combat target through GetEnemy: a recent direct attacker takes priority, followed by the siege/squad target and the previous valid enemy. Perception checks every enemy, so a nearer hidden enemy cannot prevent observation of another. Ordinary hidden positions are never refreshed from the current entity position. Teammates, radio backup and siege participants receive the last observed position with its original timestamp; sharing does not renew a sighting.

When the target is hidden, defense advances to that remembered position without a minimum firing distance. A hidden-target squad uses a column anchored at the remembered position, without the visible-target 550-unit gap. Cover requires line of sight and ends when sight is lost. With no known position, the actor stops rather than navigating to the hidden entity's current position.

A fixed 1000-unit combat radius (SERVER, no setting) protects a living combat actor from ordinary population removal/recycling and NextBot unstuck teleports while any living known enemy is within that radius, inclusive. It also gates the final respawn operation after asynchronous spawn search. Sieges remain busy until finished. Outside the radius the ordinary unseen timeout and eligibility rules apply. Death, admin cleanup and disabling the addon/type retain their separate paths.

The 60-second search timeout uses the actor's observation/report timestamp, including its original age when shared. Rewriting an NPC's engine memory to steer pursuit does not renew that timeout. Wanted and always-visible exceptions remain. Body replacement transfers the remembered position, timestamp, stable target and recent attacker. Metrocop equipment uses the same selected target as combat, with the existing arrest-target fallback. Both NextBot unstuck teleport paths check the combat radius; normal movement and optional jumps remain available. See the combat decision tree.

docs.title: Reaction to weapons in hands
docs.text:
bgn_react_to_lethal_weapon is a SERVER setting, 0 by default. When enabled, once per second living residents/police actors inspect players, NPCs and NextBots, including BGN actors. A target holding a learned lethal weapon must be within 800 units inclusive, in front of the observer's eyes (FOV, including NextBot observers), and visible through LOS. Shared-team targets, existing enemies, ignored players and players in friend mode are skipped; peaceful mode disables reactions.

The actor picks GetReactionForDamage(target) (at_damage), as when hurt. ignore/none adds no enemy. Otherwise it requests AddEnemy(target, reaction); if accepted, it stores the reaction and, while calm, clears its targets and enters that state. Busy actors retain their state. Enemy-controller, team, arrest, medic and addon-hook restrictions still apply. This starts the ordinary FSM/GOAP behavior without fabricating damage, conflict records or a wanted assignment. Later police calls and enemy sharing use their ordinary rules; the 800-unit/FOV gate applies to initial detection, not those separate systems. Holstering the weapon or disabling the setting does not clear enemies; ordinary forgetting still applies.

Learning is always active, including with the checkbox off. On BGN_OnKilledActor, SERVER checks the attacker's callable GetActiveWeapon, validates its returned entity and stores its GetClass(). The last damage must identify that same attacker. Explosion/vehicle damage and kills by a player inside a vehicle are excluded. No prefilled weapon list is supplied; the first qualifying kill teaches a class. Classification uses the weapon held at death, not the projectile/inflictor's class.

systems/sv_lethal_weapons.lua reads data/background_npcs/lethal_weapons.json once into a persistent SERVER cache, retained through script reloads. The JSON object maps class names to true; all maps share the file. Each new class updates the cache and rewrites the full object; duplicate kills and detection perform no file reads/writes. CLIENT receives only the setting through the existing cvar synchronization. An invalid file is reported and preserved without overwriting for that cache's lifetime; a write failure is reported while the learned class remains in memory. Offline edits take effect on the next server/map start. Isolated tests: tests/sv_lethal_weapons.lua via bgn_selftest.

docs.title: Panic and threat search
docs.text:
bgn_threat_search is a SERVER setting, 0 by default (Behavior → AI, Classic → Extensions). When enabled, one tick after BGN_OnKilledActor (after the ordinary witness reactions to the killing damage), SERVER looks for calm living allies of the victim (shared team, not in a vehicle, no enemy in the killer) that see the death and not the killer: within 1500 units of the victim, a clear MASK_BLOCKLOS trace from the victim's position to the actor's eyes (no view cone; the body itself is filtered out), and Combat.CanWitness(actor, killer, true) false. One who sees the killer is left to the ordinary witness reactions. The spawner never recycles or teleports an actor in panic or search_threat. Peaceful mode, ignored killers, non-combatant killers and deaths in a vehicle start nothing.

  • Residents that are neither police nor medics enter panic: a scream, a run to a route point hidden from the killer's position (bgNPC.FindCover now also takes a position), crouching there; after 15-25 s, RandomState.
  • Police and bandits (gangs included) enter search_threat: they go to a random route point within 200 units of where the killer stood, then patrol random points within 600 units of it (a new point on arrival or after 10 s); they walk instead of running within 1000 units of the killer. The search ends after 45 s or when the killer dies.

The incident keeps the class of the killer's weapon at the moment of the kill (GetActiveWeapon; a weapon in bgn_arrest_safe_weapons, no weapon, or a player in a vehicle count as none). With a class, anyone holding it is a suspect, not only the killer: an innocent with the same weapon can be attacked. Without one, only the killer is recognized in person. Allies, ignored entities and players in friend mode are never suspects. Every 0.33 s (no faster than the brain update: 0.2 s near players, 1 s far away) the actor checks entities within 500 units: distance, view cone, then Vision.HasLineOfSight last. The same suspect in 3 checks in a row is recognized; a miss or another suspect starts over. search_threat then adds it with GetReactionForDamage (ignore/none → defense), panic with run_from_danger. A recognized player alone hears sound/background_npcs/threat_alert.wav from the actor at 60% volume (EmitSound with a one-player RecipientFilter); NPCs and other players hear nothing. A refused AddEnemy keeps the state. An enemy from another system (a shot, enemy sharing) ends either state as an attack does. Isolated tests: tests/sv_threat_search.lua via bgn_selftest.

docs.title: Donor animations
docs.text:
bgNPC.Animator plays gestures using a server-owned invisible donor model and clientside bone-merged copies of the character and its weapon. It requires compatible skeletons. Ordinary static sequences still play directly on the actor's body.

The server checks active animation viewers every 0.25 seconds and sends the current animation when a ready player enters its PVS, including late connections. One-shot animations retain their original deadline; loops last until stopped. Stopping releases an NPC schedule frozen by Animator if it is still current and no static actor animation owns the body. The client copies skin, bodygroups, color, material, submaterials and model scale at animation start; subsequent appearance changes are not tracked. The dance state starts its animation after the previous state's animation is reset.

SERVER Animator.Play normally requires a PVS viewer at startup. settings.require_pvs = false permits a gameplay animation without one; room sieges use it so a closed visibility portal does not prevent deployment. Late viewers still receive the remaining animation with its original deadline.

docs.title: Bodies
docs.text:
bgn_actor_body npc|nextbot (default npc; the old value auto is the same as npc). By default actors are real HL2 NPCs (NPCBody), like in the old versions: other addons (model replacers, ragdoll and death mods, Bio-Annihilation 2, Followers) see only real NPCs (IsNPC, OnNPCKilled). With nextbot, on maps with a NavMesh, actors of the HL2 classes npc_citizen, npc_metropolice and npc_combine_s spawn as bgn_nextbot (NextBot, NextBotBody), and such addons may not work with them. The NextBot walks with the NavMesh path follower, opens doors (the ones allowed, see navigation.md "Doors"), gets unstuck, and shoots or hits with a real HL2 weapon held in its hand (players can't pick it up while the bot is alive; it drops the weapon on death, like an HL2 NPC). Shots start at the bot's right hand. The config weapon_skill works for NextBots too: the spread scales like the HL2 NPC cone (poor ×1.4, average ×1, good ×0.67, very good ×0.33, perfect ×0.2). HL2 NPCs that the bot hates are told to hate it back.

In nextbot mode, SERVER counts each foreign HL2 NPC's dispositions towards all server players and applies the most frequent disposition (D_HT, D_FR, D_LI, D_NU or D_ER) to nearby BGN NextBot bodies. Ties and an empty player list resolve to D_NU. systems/sv_nextbot_hostility.lua refreshes this once per second within 2500 units, including changes away from hostility. Initialization uses the same vote for NextBot targets. Foreign NPC dispositions towards ordinary HL2 NPC actor bodies are preserved; detection reads their direct disposition towards the actor (see wanted and conflicts). No hidden probe NPCs are created. HL2 NPC senses detect bgn_nextbot through FL_OBJECT, set before engine registration in Initialize. The periodic update is skipped in peaceful mode and with bgn_ignore_another_npc.

After updating from the probe-based implementation, reload the map to clear legacy probes. bgn_selftest includes the player-disposition vote checks; mixed-player votes are pure logic tests.

Without a weapon some models (Combine soldiers) have no plain idle/walk/run and would T-pose, so the bot falls back to the armed ones (ACT_IDLE_SMG1, ACT_WALK_RIFLE, ACT_RUN_RIFLE, then the pistol ones). Jumps are off by default (bgn_nextbot_jump, behavior settings): outside the protected combat radius a stuck bot waits and then teleports to the next path point, and a car hit only throws it. With the cvar on, a stuck bot jumps first and a hit adds a jump. An actor leaving a car is put at a spot free for its whole body, never inside the car.

docs.title: Weapons and teams
docs.text:
• Only actors whose weapon roll passed (getting_weapon_chance, 10% of citizens) are armed.
  • An unarmed actor in fear / run_from_danger runs to a free weapon within 500 units (pick_up_weapon) and fights with it. It was spawned without a weapon, so it always shoots with WEAPON_PROFICIENCY_POOR (actor.novice_shooter, bgNPC.Combat.ApplyWeaponSkill). The same goes for an HL2 NPC that picked a weapon up by its engine AI.
  • A direct attacker with no shared team is added as an enemy on the first hit, even during an existing fight; reaction hooks can still cancel it.
  • Actors of one team never damage or answer each other. bgn_team_damage 1 lets the damage through, they still don't react to it.
  • Team protection: nothing removes a civilian's residents team, vehicle collisions included (wanted). Ordinary friendly hits/kills do not start fear, retaliation or wanted. bgn_team_damage affects health only.
  • Shared enemies (systems/sv_enemy_sharing.lua, bgn_enemy_share_period, default 2 s, 0 = off): an actor with enemies (not in fear, not in a vehicle) tells every teammate within 1000 units that sees it (a trace from the teammate's eyes to the actor) about the enemies the teammate does not know. A teammate in a car is skipped, except an officer: it gets the enemy and steps out or fires from the car (modules/dv/sv_move_to_target.lua). A teammate in a calm state switches to its GetReactionForProtect reaction; a busy one only gets the enemy. This keeps the others from walking around while an officer already shoots at a player who is not wanted yet. Gang exceptions (all visible allies, without a distance cap or reaction roll) are described under gangs.
  • A wanted actor (Actor:IsWanted, wanted is lost by NPCs exactly like by players) hides: a defense reaction turns into retreat, which fights back only when the enemy is within 190 units; defense returns to retreat when the enemy is over 300 units away and the actor has under 50% of its max health. Witness check (same timer): a calm actor not in a vehicle that sees a teammate in fear, run_from_danger or dyspnea_danger with enemies, and itself sees one of that teammate's enemies within 1000 units, takes the enemy too and reacts like a calm one that was asked for help. Fights and other danger states do not count. The scan starts from scared actors within 2500 units of a living player, so no traces are spent far from players. It needs both lines of sight, so a scared actor's panic spreads only as far as eyes reach. AddEnemy guards (arrest protection, ignored entities, peaceful mode) still apply.

Prop-chair seating (sit_to_chair) uses the configured chair models and offsets. The route handles the distant approach; within 300 units the body finishes moving to the chair, and seating begins within 60 units. This applies to both HL2 NPC and NextBot bodies. Custom map seats use sit_to_chair_2.

docs.title: Choosing a brain
docs.text: bgn_brain auto|fsm|goap (default fsm, the classic brain). In auto an actor gets the brain from its config field brain = 'fsm' | 'goap', otherwise GOAP when the config has weapons, otherwise FSM.

docs.title: FSM brain
docs.text: Runs the update callback of the current state (bgNPC.States), and picks a random state from at_random when the actor has none. Reactions to damage and threats are random picks from at_damage / at_protect.

docs.title: GOAP brain
docs.text:
Plans only the fight; everything else is the FSM brain. The config reactions (at_damage / at_protect, a weighted random pick, the same as in FSM) decide whether the actor fights at all: an officer that rolled arrest arrests, a citizen that rolled fear runs. The plan takes over once the actor is in defense (or retreat, the defense of a wanted actor) and keeps it until the enemies are gone or the state leaves the plan's own states (the FSM ended the fight, an arrest, a calm state); it never pulls the actor back into a fight. Having an enemy alone (shared enemies, a wanted target) does not start one. Earlier 2.3.1 builds also picked the reactions from the plan and attacked whenever the actor had an enemy, which made fights much more frequent than with FSM.

  • Facts are measured by sensors once per second (and right after damage or a new enemy): has_enemy, armed, is_police, low_health, enemy_close, enemy_armed, enemy_police, police_called, wanted, in_cover, backup_called, outnumbered, surrendered, desperate, can_hold_door, enemy_bracing, can_siege. outnumbered is police only: two or more living enemies of the officer within 2000 units, and more of them than living officers there (itself included).
  • Actions run states: attack → defense, flee → fear, call_police → calling_police, hide → retreat (wanted actors only), take_cover → take_cover, call_backup → call_backup, surrender → arrest_surrender, hold_door → hold_door, breach_door → breach_door, siege → siege. An actor can only use actions whose state appears in its at_damage / at_protect config with a weight above zero, except actions registered with always = true (hide, take_cover, call_backup, surrender, hold_door, breach_door, siege). A trait action is rolled once per actor: call_police with its config share (20 of 100 → 20%). surrender is not a trait: it is rolled at every attempt (8%, see below). An action stays running while its state moves on to a follow-up (also, e.g. fear → run_from_danger). Any state change re-reads the facts at once, so an action that finished with its effects (take_cover sets in_cover, call_backup sets backup_called) moves the plan on instead of failing. An action whose state is already running (also after a replan) counts as entered. An action whose state moves to another action's state without its effects is blocked for 5 s, then the plan is made again; a state outside the plan ends the fight.
  • Reactions (GetReactionForDamage / GetReactionForProtect) are the config roll, as in FSM. In fear an armed actor switches to defense (as in FSM) unless the plan itself sent it to flee.
  • Chains. Fighting an armed enemy or, for an outnumbered officer, a crowd costs more out of cover, and an outnumbered officer without backup pays more again, so the plans are take_cover → attack and, for an outnumbered officer, take_cover → call_backup → attack (no cover found: call_backup → attack in the open):
  • take_cover: runs to the nearest nav point within 1000 units the enemy can't see at crouch height (bgNPC.FindCover), crouches 3 s, then fights 10 s (in_cover) before the next cover. No cover found: it fights.
  • call_backup: the outnumbered officer calls on the radio (police_backup); up to 3 free officers on foot within 4000 units take the enemy and come, and with bgn_enable_wanted_mode on every enemy of the officer (except police) becomes wanted, which sends all the police after it. Once per officer per minute. Earlier 2.3.1 builds called backup against any armed enemy, without the wanted status.
  • surrender: a hurt gangster (low_health) facing the police gives up (goal give_up, above hiding) when an officer within 700 units sees it and bgn_arrest_mode is on, and only with an 8% roll per attempt (a failed roll blocks the action for 5 s, so the roll repeats every few seconds while the conditions hold): it says give_up, the officer (stepping out of its car if needed) arrests it through ArrestModule:Surrender (systems/arrest). The plan never interrupts arrest_surrender.
  • Arrests are not planned: the arrest system (systems/arrest, ArrestModule:CanArrest) owns them, and it only works on police without enemies.
  • Goals (eliminate, survive, report, hide, give_up, shelter) get a priority from the actor's set: police, gangster or citizen (by team, or the config field goap_set). hide outranks ordinary combat while wanted; an available door shelter has priority 30 when desperate. A citizen reports (calls the police) an enemy farther than 700 units even when it is armed, unless it is hurt (then it runs) or armed itself (then it fights).
  • The planner (A* over fact bit masks) returns the cheapest action chain for the top goal. Plans are cached.
  • ignore in a reaction table keeps its random chance.

Debug: bgn_goap_debug prints the set, goal, plan and facts of the actor you look at.

docs.title: Door shelter and breaching
docs.text:
These are server-driven actions for both NPC and NextBot bodies, not random scenic poses. Any non-police GOAP actor already fighting or fleeing can seek an open door when below 35% health, unarmed against an armed enemy, or facing more living enemies within 1000 units than itself plus nearby armed teammates. An ordinary flee reaction only borrows GOAP to seek shelter; it does not become an attack if no door fits or shelter ends.

hold_door searches within 400 units for an unlocked, unclaimed rotating door. It uses the leaf's closed geometry, moves to the side away from the enemy, stays outside the swing while closing, temporarily locks the door, then steps up and plays a supported doorbracer_* sequence. Approaching takes at most 10 s, closing/positioning 4 s, holding 12 s; another attempt waits 20 s. The action ends if the enemy dies, reaches the same side, disappears from the actor's enemies, or the door is removed. It releases its lock on exit. Models are never replaced to obtain an animation: without a supported brace sequence the action is unavailable. Supported doors are upright, unparented prop_door_rotating and func_door_rotating; sliding and moving-parent doors are skipped. Physics/world obstructions may prevent reaching or closing a door, ending the attempt.

Police with an enemy actively holding the other side can choose breach_door within 800 units. They approach, kick (when the model has a suitable sequence), and open the door at 900 degrees/s, restoring its previous speed after 0.4 s. This only releases the holding actor's temporary lock; it does not force arbitrary map-locked doors.

The holder enters knocked_down: a temporary server ragdoll receives the impulse, while the same original NPC/NextBot entity and actor/UID remain registered, hidden, non-solid and unable to move, shoot or board a car. The breach and physics contacts add no damage. Shots at the ragdoll are forwarded to the actor; lethal damage uses ordinary death/corpse handling. After 3 s it looks for a full standing hull within 96 units of the body; if blocked, it stays down and retries. On recovery it restores visibility, collision, equipment and the previous combat/flee behavior, keeping current health. Removing the temporary ragdoll also removes its hidden actor. Clients only display the server state/body; they do not choose actions or control doors.

docs.title: Sieging a single-exit room
docs.text:
SERVER GOAP fighters of class npc_metropolice or npc_combine_s can choose siege for an enemy last seen within 30 s, at a doorway within 1000 units. Enemy memory stores the last visible position; the tactic does not aim at a continuously updated position through walls. It requires a loaded NavMesh, including when pedestrian routes use the custom provider. Removing the doorway connections must leave a roofed pocket containing the remembered position, with no alternate connection around the cut. Adjacent door leaves count as one exit; narrow walled NavMesh passages without door entities are also considered if door candidates do not prove a pocket. If the target vanished within 300 units of a doorway and the remembered side proves no pocket, the far side of that doorway is tried as the pocket. An actor already inside the pocket never joins; a member that enters it leaves the siege for defense without cancelling the others. Searches are bounded to 128 areas, 900 units and one floor (80-unit height tolerance); ladders, unknown geometry, missing navigation or an unproven pocket decline the tactic. The scenic indoor check alone does not prove one exit. Incomplete NavMeshes can omit real escapes such as windows or jumps.

One reservation controls the enemy/entrance. Up to five members of the initiating squad occupy separated positions outside it; other armed fighting teammates within 2000 units receive spaced waiting positions at least 650 units away (34-unit arrival tolerance). Existing squad membership is captured before the normal squad rebuild excludes siege participants. Without a current squad, the nearest eligible allies fill the five places. Only actors with a supported waiting animation join. Positioning has a 15 s limit; the 12 s silent wait starts after the front group is positioned and rear participants have withdrawn. Both NPC and NextBot bodies suppress ordinary shooting during the tactic; siege radio lines remain enabled. Followers can execute the state with an FSM brain; the initiating fighter requires GOAP.

An officer holding fire for negotiation cannot initiate or join a siege. Negotiation also excludes actors already in a siege, so the two systems cannot restore each other's weapon capabilities.

Narrow corridors fall back to separated positions along the passage instead of side positions. Members that cannot fit near the entrance try the rear positions; if a close eligible reinforcement cannot withdraw, the attempt ends rather than leaving an uncoordinated group crowding the active siege.

After waiting, closed rotating doors are kicked with 35% probability or opened normally. An unsupported kick falls back to a supported opening gesture, and vice versa; without either animation the doorway is unavailable. Combine models can use their gun strike to breach. Existing door-opening/locked-door settings and held-door reservations still apply. The operator steps outside the swing and retries opening once if necessary. Doors must have started opening before deployment, and the payload path must be clear. Their automatic return delay is temporarily suspended and restored on exit; a previously locked door is relocked after the attempt. Door entities are preserved.

The single operator deploys one npc_manhack (npc_metropolice, requires deploy) or one npc_grenade_frag (npc_combine_s, requires grenThrow). The selected model is never replaced. Existing donor animation playback prevents native NPC animation events from creating duplicate weapons. The grenade uses a traced ballistic path, a 3.5 s fuse and a blast-clearance check for non-enemy actors/players. The manhack gets a checked entry direction and two seconds of native directed flight, then ordinary AI; it is hostile (D_HT) to every current enemy of the operator, friendly (D_LI) to the operator's team, neutral (D_NU) to everyone else, never becomes wanted, is skipped by the relationship and NextBot-hostility updaters that would override its relations, and removes itself after 30 s. Weapon damage is attributed to its operator. The operator opens the door and releases the weapon from the same spot: the throw starts while the leaf is still swinging (a retry window of 1.5 s covers a blocked path), and the operator then returns to its slot during the fuse. The operator is not part of the blast-clearance check. The group holds another 6 s after deployment. The whole attempt is limited to 50 s and shares a 60 s target cooldown. Damage to a participant, loss of an enemy/operator, leaving the pocket, interruption by arrest or another state, map cleanup or a navigation reload ends it and restores body control. Clients display the state/animations; they do not choose the tactic or spawn weapons.

docs.title: Hostage negotiation
docs.text:
systems/sv_negotiation.lua (SERVER). A frightened non-police actor within 100 units of a player target that stands closer to the officer than the target is a hostage: the target hides behind it, so approaching from behind does not count. Every officer whose selected target meets this rule holds fire (engine NPCs lose CAP_USE_WEAPONS, NextBots skip UpdateCombat), the first one offers to surrender and warns 5 s before the 20 s deadline. A negotiating officer in defense keeps its distance: closer than 600 units it stops approaching (squad slots included), closer than 400 it backs off. The talks end quietly when the shield stays gone for 3 s; they fail on the deadline or when the player kills anyone. After a failure the officers shoot again and the player is not offered talks until he is arrested, drops a wanted level, dies or 120 s pass. Negotiation with NPC targets is a separate story scenario and is not implemented.

The hostage test currently uses radius, fear state and relative distance only; it does not check LOS to the hostage or alignment with the firing line. This rule has not been changed by the combat audit fixes.

docs.title: Extending
docs.text:
bgNPC.GOAP.RegisterAction('duck', {
    state = 'retreat',                      -- a registered state that performs the action
    pre = { has_enemy = true, enemy_armed = true },
    effects = { safe = true },
    cost = function(ws) return 1 end,       -- number or function(world_state)
    -- optional: always = true (no config weight needed), trait = true + chance = 0.3 (rolled once per actor),
    -- prepare = function(actor) return true end (sets up before the state starts; false blocks the action)
})
bgNPC.GOAP.sensors.my_fact = function(actor, npc, enemy) return ... end
bgNPC.GOAP.RegisterSet('my_set', { survive = function(ws) return 10 end })

docs.title: Squads
docs.text: bgn_module_tactical_groups (on by default). Every second actors in defense of one team within 1200 units form squads of up to 5. The healthiest leads, its selected combat enemy becomes the target of every member. Formations face the target: column when nobody sees it, wedge with 4+ healthy members, line otherwise. The healthiest stand in front, the wounded (< 40% health) form a rear rank. defense moves a member to actor.squad.slot; bgNPC.Squads.list holds the current squads.

docs.title: LOD
docs.text:
Actors far from players update less often (bgn_lod_near_radius); idle unarmed actors out of range sleep (bgn_disable_logic_radius). Hook: BGN_ActorLODChanged(actor, lod) (1 near, 2 far, 3 dormant).

Distant unseen unarmed actors on foot now alternate pauses and active windows instead of remaining frozen. SERVER settings (Performance and classic Optimization): bgn_logic_pause = 2 s (0 disables pauses), bgn_logic_active = 1 s (minimum 0.1), bgn_logic_stagger = 0.25 s per UID. During active windows both engine movement and the brain resume; brain interval is 0.2 s. Phase is (time - UID * stagger) modulo (pause + active), stable across list reordering. Windows overlap and phases wrap in larger crowds; this spreads transitions, not exclusive execution. Close/in-view actors, armed actors and vehicle occupants retain continuous simulation. Damage/enemy events immediately wake an actor for at least one second. LOD 3 now means intermittent simulation, not permanent sleep. Existing distance thresholds are retained; with near radius 2500 and disable radius 500, off-view actors beyond 2500 enter this cycle. Timings are observed on actor scheduler passes, not exact real-time deadlines.

docs.title: Medics
docs.text:
Actor type medic (config/actors/sh_medic.lua, limit 4: two pairs) is never spawned by the regular spawner. Every actor death outside a vehicle is a call (bgNPC.Medics.calls, kept 90 s). A free medic takes it, otherwise one is spawned near the body, with an ambulance when Decent Vehicle is on and the config has vehicles. The ambulance drives to the body like a police car on a chase, the medic gets out, kneels over the body for 6 s with voice lines and medkit sounds (state medic_revive), the actor comes back (same type, model and skin; its ragdoll is removed) and the medic returns to the car. A call closes when the body is gone (a client reports its ragdoll faded or was cleaned up, or the server ragdoll was removed) or after 90 s; the medic then walks back to its car and drives on with the siren off. The last 300 units to the body the medic walks straight, off the nav points. Some deaths cannot be saved: explosions, vehicle hits and overkill damage always, any other death with the chance bgn_medic_hopeless_chance (25 %; Behavior > Medics). For those the medic still comes and kneels over the body, but instead of reviving says medic_cannot_save and leaves (call.verdict); only then does an officer take the body. Medics only take as enemies those who hurt them. Nobody comes for an actor killed by the police (team police), nor for one whose death no living ally of the victim saw, nor for an enemy of the residents or one whose team is fighting them.

When a medic is killed, medic spawns and responses are blocked around the death position. Existing calls in that area pause: their responders stop heading to the body and return to their ambulance when possible. bgn_medic_danger_time defaults to 60 seconds (0 disables the restriction), and bgn_medic_danger_radius defaults to 1500 units; both are in the behavior settings under Medics. The area reopens when the timer expires or the killer dies (player, NPC or NextBot actor). Areas belonging to other killers remain blocked. Pending calls can resume while their original 90-second lifetime remains; the restriction does not extend that lifetime. Hook: BGN_ActorRevived(actor, call).

  • Pairs: a medic spawned for a call brings a partner when the limit allows (medic_partner on both). It rides in the same ambulance (seats: 2), gets out with the medic, kneels beside the body (call.partner) and gets back in with it; a partner within 400 units of the car is pulled in when the medic takes the wheel.
  • Ambulances: no new one when a player near the call (3000 units) already has an ambulance around; an empty ambulance there is taken instead.
  • Attacked: by a player, the medic reviving keeps reviving (a life first) and its partner fights with fists (state brawl); a medic not reviving fights itself. Below 30 % health a medic leaves the call (the partner takes it over) and runs, by its car when one is near (go_to_police_car, then fear). Attacked by an actor, it runs as before.

docs.title: Gangs
docs.text:
Two street gangs replace the plain gangster actor (kept disabled as their config base): Black Raven (gangster_crows, team gang_crows) and Red Wolf (gangster_wolves, team gang_wolves) (config/actors/sh_gangs.lua). Both keep the team bandits (police reactions, carjacking). A member is light (35 % are heavy, heavy_chance): light members wear HL2 citizen clothes and carry a pistol, heavy ones wear rebel gear and carry an SMG or a rifle (systems/npcs/sv_gang_models.lua). The clothes sheet of the model is replaced by the gang's recolor with SetSubMaterial (materials/background_npcs/gangs/<gang>/<class>_<sex>); the class is read from the model, so it survives revival and leaving a car. The recolors are made from the game's own textures by tools/make_gang_skins.py (needs vpk, srctools, pillow, numpy); the game files are not shipped.

Gang support and walking. Members walk in packs of up to three; all visible same-gang allies receive a threat without a chance roll or roster cap, including late arrivals. Combat support is independent of walking packs. See gangs for visibility, sharing interval and war rules.

Orphan bodies: Actor:RemoveActor leaves the entity to the engine, right for a death only. Every 2 s an NPC or NextBot that is an actor body (BGN_ACTOR_OBJECT, or bgn_npc_class from the spawner) without a live registered actor is removed after 3 seconds, even with bgn_enable 0 (spawner/sv_actor_remover.lua, with developer 1 the console names its class, health, type and last state). Health is not checked: an NPC killed while the LOD had its think turned off, or frozen by the animator, never finishes dying and stands with 0 health, frozen, without a label; the old check (alive bodies only) left those on the map for good. An actor removed in its first tick is no longer registered afterwards (it kept a slot of the type limit). A medic marked eternal for a call is released together with the call, so it no longer escapes the limit and the remover.

Calling the police is skipped when the target is already wanted, or at least one living officer has it as an enemy or a target (bgNPC.PoliceKnows, calling_police state and the GOAP police_called sensor).

docs.title: Delay between skirmishes
docs.text: bgn_fight_cooldown (Behavior > AI, 0-120 s, default 60, 0 = off, the old behavior). With a delay, the first defense reaction of the at_protect table (actors protecting their own) opens a window of that many seconds around the place (2500 units). While it lasts, protecting against another attacker in that area is ignored: the actor takes the ignore reaction and a call for help, enemy sharing or a witnessed hit adds no enemy to it. The police are never delayed, also an officer driving past in a car. Actors joining the skirmish that opened the window (same attacker), fights already going, places outside the area and the time after the window are not affected. A player, or an NPC / NextBot of another mod that is not one of our actors, as the attacker is never blocked (systems/sv_fight_cooldown.lua).

docs.title: Police at a body
docs.text: Every actor death outside a vehicle also leaves a body for 60 s (brain/fsm/states/sv_police_inspect_body.lua). The nearest officer within 2000 units who walks or idles without enemies takes it (state police_inspect_body): runs to the body when it is farther than 600 units (walks when closer), says police_body_arrive, crouches over it, reports it on the radio (police_body_report) and writes it down (police_body_notes), 5 s each, then goes on patrolling. Bodies from a shoot-out are taken once the officers calm down; an enemy that appears during the inspection ends it at once and the officer reacts as to an attack. Bodies within 150 units are one scene with one officer. A body revived by a medic is dropped. A body a medic is on the way to waits until the medic has revived it or declared it hopeless.

docs.title: Onlookers
docs.text: Every actor death outside a vehicle is also an incident for 45 s (brain/fsm/states/sv_watch_incident.lua). From 5 s after it, calm civilians walking or idling within 1500 units come one by one (35% per 2 s check, up to 4): they stand 150-280 units from the spot on their side, stare (LineIdle*), half of them say a watch_incident line, and go on after 12-25 s. A gunshot scares them like any calm actor; two of them may start a conversation. When the medics revive the actor (BGN_ActorRevived), the incident ends: no new onlookers come and those already there go on.

docs.title: Bodies
docs.text:
systems/sv_corpses.lua, systems/cl_corpses.lua. Settings window: Behavior > Bodies.

Cvar (server) Default Meaning bgn_corpse_cleanup 0 the bodies of dead actors (NPC and NextBot) fade out (off by default) bgn_corpse_cleanup_time 60 seconds after the death

A body a medic is assigned to, or an officer is inspecting, waits until they are done (both end on their own: the call after 90 s, the inspection after its give-up time). Server ragdolls fade on the server, client ragdolls on every client. npc_battle_cleanup would remove a body in seconds, before a medic or an officer gets to it, so the actors' bodies are left to this setting: server ragdolls get its doNotRemove flag, its client-side corpse cleanup skips them. With bgn_corpse_cleanup 0 (the default) the flag is not set and npc_battle_cleanup, if installed, removes the bodies as usual; without it they stay until the engine's own ragdoll limits remove them.

docs.title: Cars
docs.text:
Police dismount when a living enemy (or their current arrest target) is within 800 units or their vehicle has at most 20% health remaining. They stay seated while that enemy is driving away: the dismount waits until the enemy's car has stood still for about 6 seconds or the enemy gets out.

A police car chasing a wanted player that falls more than 2800 units behind and is out of every player's view is not culled: its crew steps out and the car is rebuilt (a fresh car, the same actors and enemies) on a hidden road point 600-2200 units from the player, at most once per 8 seconds per player and only while fewer than 1 + wanted level chasing cars are close. See spawner/sv_police_pursuit.lua. Spawn points also keep clear of the road ahead of a moving player. Simfphys health uses GetCurHealth() and GetMaxHealth(); vehicles without a positive maximum health do not trigger the damage condition. Neutral players do not trigger dismounts. Hits use the normal actor damage reactions, so a real attack can create an enemy and make police dismount. Direct vehicle removal removes its crew; forced ejection still requires a safe exit.

Actors and Decent Vehicle cars; the state go_to_police_car (no longer police only) runs to the car and gets in.

  • Back to the car (modules/dv/sv_return_to_vehicle.lua, every 2 s): an actor within 1000 units of an allowed car returns when no enemy is within 1500 units. Neutral living players also delay civilians, but not police. Former crew may take free passenger seats after their driver returns. Police do not reboard critically damaged cars.
  • The enemy drives off (sv_defense.lua, every 2 s, 30 %): a player in a vehicle or an actor in a car; checked before the squad move, so squad members go too.
  • Confiscation and carjacking (data.seize): when no car of its own is near, the police take a car of another group ("police_seize") and bandits carjack one ("gangster_carjack"): whoever sits inside is thrown out (VEHICLE:Eject, scared unless it is a teammate) and the car joins the actor's group (VEHICLE:SetGroup: the police get the chase AI). Bandits on the run (retreat, fear, run_from_danger) within 700 units of such a car take it too (35 % per check) and keep running in it.

NextBots and cars (systems/sv_nextbot_vehicle_hits.lua): a NextBot has no physics object, so the engine deals it no crush damage. Every 0.1 s each moving car (players', Decent Vehicle ones) faster than 150 u/s hurts NextBots in its box and just ahead ((speed - 75) x 0.25, the driver is the attacker) and throws them. A NextBot whose enemy sits in a car shoots the car (the enemy is the car then, which has no health of its own).

Which car: VEHICLE:CanBoard: an empty one the actor left, or of its group (police, bandits, medics, ...), never someone else's residents car (police and medics are residents too, citizens keep to their own). Former crew may also rejoin an occupied car if a passenger seat is free. A police vehicle keeps its police designation even after a group change; only police actors may drive or ride in it. Players can still take an empty police car. VEHICLE:CanSeize: a car of another group, empty or driven by an actor (never a player), not driven by a teammate. Only the police and bandits seize.

Boarding removes the physical NPC/NextBot and binds the same logical actor to a DV anim entity; exiting recreates its original body and equipment. Exit placement prefers the closest model exit or the side and row of its own seat, checking full body clearance and overlap even with non-colliding actors. If all positions are blocked, it stays aboard. Seated hits retain the attacker and notify nearby witnesses through the normal damage hooks. Witness traces exclude their own chassis/seat and recognize another occupant's chassis; walls still block sight.

BGN traffic can plan bounded forward/reverse maneuvers around blockers and, after repeated failures, try another accessible road segment. Red lights, scheduled stops and taxi waits suppress recovery. Cars honk briefly only at an entity blocking their forward sensor. These changes apply to BGN-created vehicles; DV remains required. See traffic checks and limitations.

docs.title: Related systems
docs.text: Gangs walk in packs of three and support visible allies; direct self-defense remains. Medics and bodies own calls/verdicts/cleanup. Wanted and arrest own pursuit/surrender. Stuck NextBots choose nearby free navigation space excluding vehicles; custom-chair placement uses seat height.

docs.title: Police weapon choice and witnessed harm
docs.text: See police weapon choice and harm memory.

docs.title: NextBot pistol cadence
docs.text:
The stock pistol now fires groups of 1–3 individual shots, approximately 0.2 s apart, followed by a 0.45–0.8 s rest. These are separate, visibility/friendly-fire-checked shots, not multiple bullets in one attack. The 18-round magazine keeps the 1.8 s reload pause. Burst state resets on weapon/target changes and reload; other weapon profiles and scripted-weapon fallback remain unchanged. Combat checks quantize the intended intervals to engine ticks.

python tools/test_police_force.py checks witnessed distinct counts, thresholds, memory/reset/rebind, vehicle damage and pistol cadence. Live single-player checks compare native HL2 and NextBot shots and inspect arrest weapon retention; multiplayer and third-party weapon bases require separate verification.

Movement updates run every 0.1 s for near actors and every 0.25 s for far or dormant ones (the node arrival radius is 150 units).

docs.title: Conversations, fights and staring
docs.text: Code: lua/background_npcs_core/systems/dialogue/sv_conversation.lua. Off with bgn_disable_dialogues 1.

docs.title: Conversations
docs.text:
An actor in a calm state may enter the dialogue state (its at_random weight). It looks for free calm actors within 400 units in sight and picks a script all of them fit (weighted by chance). They walk to places around a point (8 s at most), face each other and say the lines one after another with gestures. Text appears over the speaker's head, the voice plays on clients that have it on (Voices). Anything that changes one participant's state (danger, damage) ends the conversation for all.

SERVER suppresses random state phrases and ambient coughs for all participants while gathering, talking or reacting to a player's interruption. These resume after the actor leaves the conversation; scripted lines and the conversation's player reactions still play normally on CLIENT.

Scripts: config/states/sh_conversations.lua, phrases: bgNPC.cfg.replics['conv_<id>'] in each language file.

table.insert(bgNPC.cfg.conversations, {
    id = 'my_talk',                        -- bgNPC.cfg.replics['conv_my_talk'] = { ... 3 phrases ... }
    roles = { 'police', { 'citizen', 'taxi_driver' } }, -- actor types, 2 or 3 participants
    lines = { { 1 }, { 2, 'scared' }, { 1, 'angry' } }, -- { speaker role, mood }: talk wave angry laugh scared
    final = 'flee',                        -- optional, see below
    chance = 10,                           -- relative weight, default 10
})
final What happens (none) they go back to their business; a player may interrupt fight roles 1 and 2 start a fist fight attack role 2 opens fire on role 1 (and role 1 fights back) flee role 2 runs from role 1. Police as role 1: half the time the suspect gives up and is arrested, otherwise the police open fire run_off role 1 runs off somewhere

The self-test conversations.scripts checks that every script has as many phrases as lines.

docs.title: Interrupting
docs.text: A player within 250 units who looks at an ordinary conversation (no final) for 2 s interrupts it with a 50% chance, once per conversation: they turn to the player and one of them tells them off (conv_interrupt, police_interrupt, gangster_interrupt).

docs.title: Staring
docs.text:
A player within 350 units staring at someone standing still (idle, random_gesture):

Staring Reaction 3 s turns to the player and says something (stare_1) 7 s warns (stare_2) 11 s gangsters and thieves start a fist fight, civilians half the time (otherwise walk away); police only warn

The police and gangster variants are police_stare_* and gangster_stare_*.

docs.title: Fist fights
docs.text: The brawl state (group assault): no weapons, the hits change health directly, so they are not damage events: nobody calls it a murder, nobody gets wanted, the police don't shoot. An NPC that drops to 35% health gives up and runs; a player is beaten down to 15 HP, never killed (a player's own fist hits on the fighter land, without the usual reaction). A police officer who sees a fight (arrest mode on) arrests both fighters one after another; NPC fighters give up and wait (arrest_surrender). The fight ends after 45 s or at 800 units apart.

docs.title: Gangs and combat pacing
docs.text: Server sources: config/actors/sh_gangs.lua, systems/sv_fight_roster.lua, systems/sv_enemy_sharing.lua, systems/sv_fight_cooldown.lua, systems/npcs/sv_gang_pack.lua, sv_gang_models.lua.

docs.title: Gang identity
docs.text:
gangster_crows (Black Raven) and gangster_wolves (Red Wolf) inherit gangster. Each has gang = 'crows'|'wolves' and teams bandits plus gang_<id>. Both are enabled, each with fullness = 5 (5% of bgn_max_npc). Light members use pistols and citizen clothing; 35% heavy members use rebel equipment and SMG/AR2. Gang model selection also applies to NextBot bodies. Models/materials are shipped in the addon.

Gangsters of every gang type (gangster and both gangs; respawn_delay = 30 is inherited from gangster) come back no sooner than 30 seconds after a death of their type, one per 30 seconds. racer_driver also inherits gangster but sets respawn_delay = 0. Both spawners read the resolved (inherited) config.

Gang alliance uses gang identity, not the common bandits tag: rivals do not join one another's protection calls. Police/car access still uses team rules.

docs.title: Clothing textures
docs.text:
Black Raven wears worn charcoal leather and graphite fabric with raven patches; Red Wolf uses burgundy canvas, dark reinforcements and wolf patches. Trousers, boots and equipment retain separate material colors. The eight painted sheets cover both sexes and light/heavy equipment, using the original HL2 UV layout. Heavy equipment uses gang insignia in place of resistance and medical markings.

The SERVER selects the model and applies SetSubMaterial; CLIENT rendering uses the shipped VMT/VTF assets. Editable PNG sheets live in tools/gang_skins/<gang>/<class>_<sex>.png. Run python tools/make_gang_skins.py (Pillow and srctools) to rebuild the VTF files with their existing dimensions, flags and mipmaps; it no longer recolors the game's textures.

docs.title: Fight roster
docs.text:
The capped roster has been replaced by visible-ally support (systems/sv_enemy_sharing.lua). Every living same-gang member that sees an ally outside the fear state with a living enemy receives that enemy. Calm members enter defense (wanted members use retreat) without a chance roll, roster cap or protection cooldown. Walking packs and distance do not limit support: an unobstructed line of sight to the ally is required (a trace, without a facing-direction check). Threats can spread through visible allies. Late arrivals also join; seeing the enemy itself is unnecessary. Seated members also receive enemies. Busy members receive the enemy without changing their current state; arrest protection and state locks remain in effect.

Checks run every bgn_enemy_share_period seconds (default 2, 0 disables sharing), outside peaceful mode. bgn_gang_help_chance remains for compatibility but no longer affects support. The random 2–6-member roster has been removed.

A calm member can start a rival-gang fight within 700 units with direct line of sight, checked every 10 seconds with bgn_gang_war_chance (default 0.5%, 0 disables).

docs.title: Pack walking
docs.text: Living members of the same gang, regardless of their current state, form packs of up to three, in entity-index order. Each member joins the first pack with a free slot and a leader within 1500 units, or leads a new pack. The leader chooses its route normally. Its two followers stay 80–180 units around its current position, match its pace (walk or run), and recheck the pack every 2 seconds. Singles/pairs remain when there are not enough eligible members. Combat can unite multiple walking packs. Following runs in the walk state; a member in another state can still lead, so followers may gather around a stationary ally.

docs.title: Protection cooldown
docs.text:
bgn_fight_cooldown defaults to 60 seconds, 0 disables. The first protection defense reaction opens a window within 2500 units. During it, protection against another actor attacker in that area is ignored, without adding that enemy. Joining against the same attacker is allowed. Player attacks and foreign NPC/NextBot attackers are never delayed; direct self-defense is unaffected. Police are never delayed, including an officer driving past in a car. A blocked witness gets no enemy whether it was calm or already busy. This is event pacing, not a global pause of ongoing combat. Enemy sharing between visible gang allies bypasses this cooldown.

These cvars are server settings; definitions: cvars/sh_cvars.lua. For baseline civilian/police reactions see brains.

docs.title: Ghost crowd (experimental)
docs.text:
Garry's Mod can't afford hundreds of real NPCs. The ghost crowd fills the far distance with cheap client-side figures (ClientsideModel) that look and behave like the real actors near you, in the spirit of the "Legion" system from Serious Sam 4. Local mode only requests navigation points from the server; server mode also runs and synchronizes ghost movement.

Two modes:

The ghost crowd is off by default (bgn_ghost_crowd 0, bgn_cl_ghost_crowd 0); turn it on in the menu or choose the New mode. A ghost that a player sees never fades next to them: it runs away (or, on the server, becomes a real actor).

  • Server (bgn_ghost_crowd 1): the server runs the ghosts, every player sees the same ones, and a ghost a player walks up to becomes a real actor on its spot. The client settings then do nothing (locked in the menu with a note).
  • Local (bgn_ghost_crowd 0 and bgn_cl_ghost_crowd 1): every client may invent its own ghosts. They change nothing in the game, players see different ones, and a ghost can't be caught: it runs away or fades.
Cvar Default Meaning bgn_cl_ghost_crowd (client) 0 local mode: enable the ghost crowd bgn_cl_ghost_crowd_max (client) 40 local mode: the most ghosts at once bgn_ghost_crowd (server) 0 server mode bgn_ghost_crowd_max (server) 40 server mode: the most ghosts at once, shared fairly between the players

Settings window: My settings → Experimental (client), Spawn → Experimental (server).

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Where: in a ring from 0.35 to 1.5 × bgn_spawn_radius around the player, never inside that inner radius around any player (real actors live there, multiplayer included). They appear out of sight, with a fade-in. At the limit a ghost behind the player moves into view, so open areas don't look empty.
  • Looks: model, skin and bodygroups of real actors you have seen; HL2 citizens until then. Models without a walk or an idle animation (vehicles, helicopters, some custom models) are skipped.
  • Mood: taken from the real actors around you once a second. Panic when 20% or more of them are in the danger or assault state group, or retreating (one scared actor matters more than a dozen walkers), or when someone wanted is within the ghosts' ring. It lasts 10 s after the last cause; a new panic makes every ghost drop its goal and run (half of the ghosts run upright, the rest crouched, picked once per ghost). States are registered on the server only, so the actor sync sends the group too (actor.state_group on the client). Calm ghosts walk, some stand for a while (the share follows actors in idle).
  • Movement: point to point (up to 700 units, a wall trace per step), feet on the ground (a trace down every 0.15 s, nav points often hang above it), never towards the player: sideways is allowed when calm, only away in panic. Ghosts don't enter the inner radius.
  • Leaving: when the player gets inside the inner radius a ghost out of sight is removed at once, a seen one runs away; it fades out only when the player is very close or it has nowhere to go. Real actors spawn in that area instead.

docs.title: Server mode
docs.text:
• Same for everyone: a ghost walks segments { from, to, t0, speed } (walk 75, run 190 units/s). The server sends a segment once (with the look when the ghost is new, in one message per 0.25 s for all changes); every client computes the position from CurTime() and scales the animation to that speed. A client that starts drawing (joined, switched it on, mode changed) asks for all ghosts at once.
  • Spawn, walk, leave: the local rules, checked against every player: ring of each player, out of every player's inner radius, out of everybody's sight. Mood (panic, idle share) is counted per player from the server's actor states; a ghost follows its nearest player's. Looks (type, model, skin, bodygroups) come from real actors on foot with walk and idle animations.
  • Handoff: a ghost someone sees, with a player inside its inner radius, becomes a real actor of the same type and look on its spot (dropped to the ground), facing its way. Clients keep drawing the ghost until the entity arrives (at most 2 s), so there is no gap and no double. An unseen ghost there just goes. The handoff may go over the type limit: normal recycling removes eligible excess actors only after no player has seen them for bgn_actor_unseen_time (default 30 s), including during server overload. On an overloaded server, new handoffs stay within the type limit. When the type is off (or its limit is 0) or the spawn fails, the ghost runs away and fades like a local one.

  • Not in server mode: the "ghost behind the player moves into view" at the limit.

  • systems/sh_ghost_crowd.lua: rules of both modes (next point, sight, segments, radii).

  • systems/cl_ghost_crowd.lua: ghosts, mood, movement (client); draws the server's ghosts in server mode.
  • systems/sv_ghost_crowd.lua: answers bgn_ghost_crowd_points with the nav points around the player (once per 2 s per player, up to 1500 points). Answers are cached for 15 s per 1024-unit map cell and radius, so players near each other share one navigation query. Server mode: runs the ghosts (bgn_ghost_crowd / bgn_ghost_crowd_sync messages).

bgNPC.Nav.GetPointsInRadius(center, radius, link_type, limit) takes an optional limit; the navmesh provider returns 64 points by default.

Self-test: bgn_selftest / bgn_selftest_cl → ghost_crowd_rules.

Carried ration boxes/suitcases/newspapers use the same actor carry_items config and per-type switch as real citizens. Local mode chooses a supported item on the client; server mode chooses once and sends carry with each segment/snapshot. Clients use matching walk/idle sequences and attached non-colliding models. Panic stows a parcel/newspaper or drops a suitcase for carry_items.drop_lifetime seconds (default 30); local drops are client decoration. Server handoff preserves a compatible selected/stowed item without another probability roll. HL2 NPC handoff discards parcels/newspapers and uses a client-only briefcase for a suitcase. See carry configuration.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Every ghost animates every frame; 100+ ghosts may cost noticeable FPS.
  • On a navmesh the points come from about ±256 units of height around the player, hilly maps get fewer ghosts.
  • The fade-out uses render.SetBlend in the opaque pass, which can show artifacts while fading.

docs.title: Medics and bodies
docs.text:
Server owners: systems/sv_medics.lua, systems/sv_corpses.lua, states sv_medic_revive.lua, sv_police_inspect_body.lua; client fading: systems/cl_corpses.lua.

Eligible actor deaths create calls. A free medic responds, otherwise the system can spawn one; an ambulance is optional and requires DV, configured installed vehicles and road waypoints. A call is not a guarantee of revival: availability, danger and body lifetime still apply. Medics release completed/closed calls rather than remaining assigned forever.

Server cvar Default Meaning bgn_medic_hopeless_chance 25 Percent of ordinary deaths considered hopeless. bgn_medic_danger_time 60 Avoid the area of a murdered colleague for this many seconds or until the killer dies; 0 disables. bgn_corpse_cleanup 0 Optional BGN corpse fading; disabled by default. bgn_corpse_cleanup_time 60 Seconds after death before cleanup may begin.

A call is created only when a living ally of the victim (same team) sees the body at the moment of death. Only the innocent are saved: no call for an actor at war with the residents (it counted one of them as an enemy, or one of them counted it), nor for one whose teammate is fighting the residents at that moment; residents themselves always qualify. Explosions and bullet/buckshot hits within 150 units are always hopeless. Vehicle impacts use the normal chance and can be saved. A medic gives a verdict; police can run to inspect the body. A medic en route or an officer inspecting it postpones cleanup until the activity finishes. Reviving retires the matching body record. Server ragdolls fade server-side; client ragdolls receive removal events. When BGN cleanup is disabled, it does not block npc_battle_cleanup.

Medics/ambulances are protected from police enemy/wanted/offender handling and ambulance confiscation. These are targeted service-role rules, not general invulnerability.

For seated character death and physics limits see vehicles; for verification tools see testing.

docs.title: Settings menu
docs.text:
Open it with the console command bgn_menu [page], the Background NPCs icon in the context menu (C), or Spawn menu → Options → Background NPCs → Open settings.

The window scales with the screen height and width (designed at 960 px of height, so 1080p is 1.125x; the narrower side wins, so it fits 4:3 and small screens, minimum 0.75x), has a light and a dark theme (bgn_menu_dark, also the sun / moon button) and soft interface sounds (bgn_menu_sounds). Texts follow the game language (English and Russian), or the one chosen in My settings → Menu (bgn_cl_ui_language: auto, english, russian): the chosen language's resource/localization/<lang>/bgn_*.properties are loaded over the game's. language.Add doesn't replace a phrase the game already loaded, so they are also kept in bgNPC.Phrases, which Menu.Text reads first. The interface language doesn't change the NPC phrases: they have bgn_cl_voice_language (see voices.md). Language synchronization sends only the language code to SERVER (bgn_cl_language), so server-generated Tool reports use the selected mod language as well.

The search field (Ctrl+F) looks through every page: labels, help texts and cvar names; Esc clears it. The full screen button (or a double click on the header) maximizes the window.

The sidebar has three groups: Server (settings registered with bgNPC.CVars, admins only), Only for you (the "My settings" page: this computer's options) and More ("Other works"). Non-admins don't see server settings at all: a section without visible rows has no heading, a page without visible rows is not listed. bgn_menu_as_player [1/0] (no argument toggles) shows the window as a non-admin sees it, for debugging; the server still checks the rights.

Tools → Testing runs the testing mode: spawn, vehicle, state and settings checks with a copyable log.

Spawnmenu Options → Background NPCs → Debugging collects debug overlays, NPC paths, actor WH, the state/decision inspector, sight visualization and an actor first-person camera. See debug controls.

Modules lists the switchable modules: Wanted, Arrest, Scenic NPCs, Decent Vehicle and the supported addons. The switch of a module is shown to everybody and is locked for a player who is not an admin. A gear opens the module's own page (opened from the page, not listed in the sidebar; search finds its rows) with a Server section (admins) and an Only for you section (this computer's options, e.g. the wanted HUD and halo). The gear is shown only when the player has something on that page: any server row for an admin, a client row for everybody; Decent Vehicle has server rows only while Decent Vehicle is loaded (DecentVehicleDestination). Modules → Scenic NPCs (gear) has a checkbox for each automatically eligible scene (bgn_scenic_<id>). Actors shows the vehicle count of a type with a blue Decent Vehicle badge (only while Decent Vehicle is loaded) and Spawn with carried items (bgn_carry_items_<type>) only for types with a carry_items config table. Both controls also exist in Classic settings and affect future spawning, including ghost items. Tools are split into Background NPCs: Editor (route points, spawn areas, seats) and Background NPCs: Debugging (actor inspector, navigation, movement, scenes, carried items). The debug page shares UID selection, visualization modes, distance/limit filters and freeze controls with the inspector Tool.

Behavior → AI and Classic → Extensions contain React to weapons in hands (bgn_react_to_lethal_weapon, SERVER/admin, default 0). Learning continues while off; see detection, reactions and stored weapon classes. They also contain Panic and threat search (bgn_threat_search, SERVER/admin, default 0); see panic and threat search.

docs.title: Spawn and recycling settings
docs.text:
The Spawn page holds the pedestrian settings; the vehicle visibility radius is in Modules → Decent Vehicle (gear). Server defaults:

Cvar Default Meaning bgn_spawn_period 0 Pause in seconds between spawner passes. bgn_actors_max_teleports 10 Maximum actor teleports per second. bgn_actors_teleporter 1 Move eligible unseen actors instead of removing them. bgn_spawn_radius 3000 Radius used to find spawn points around players. bgn_spawn_block_radius 600 No pedestrian spawns this close to any player. bgn_spawn_no_visibility_trace 0 Skip the pedestrian cover trace: a spawn or teleport point in any player's field of view is rejected even behind an obstacle. bgn_spawn_radius_visibility 2000 Visibility radius of players. Used only by wanted: a wanted NPC/actor (not a player) is dropped after 15 s outside every player's field of view or farther than half of this radius; obstacles are not checked. bgn_vehicle_spawn_visibility_radius 2000 Within this distance in a player's view direction vehicles spawn only when the whole car body (a grid of points over its size) is hidden behind cover; affects vehicles only. bgn_actor_unseen_time 30 Seconds unseen by every player before an eligible actor can be removed or teleported; 0 permits immediate recycling out of sight. bgn_vehicle_cleanup_time 120 Cleanup timeout for an unseen BGN car left without a driver or failing to move more than 128 units from its anchor; 0 disables this additional cleanup.

Pedestrian spawn and teleport checks test feet, chest and head against visible obstructions; vehicle spawns test a grid over the car body. A point in a player's view counts as covered only when the obstruction stops the sight line at least 40 units short of it, and the player's own car does not count as cover. Outside the view cone, points beyond the block radius remain eligible. Candidate checks do not yield midway. Busy actors (conversation, arrest, revival and scenic work), seated actors and locked states are protected from normal recycling. The unseen timeout applies to over-limit actors too; disabling the addon or an actor type follows its separate removal path. Vehicle cleanup checks the chassis against all players, including partially exposed cars and occupied seats.

docs.title: Adding a page
docs.text:
-- client side, after Background NPCs is loaded
bgNPC.Menu.AddPage('my_addon', {
    title = { en = 'My addon', ru = 'Мой аддон' },   -- or '#phrase' from resource/localization, or plain text
    icon = 'background_npcs/vgui/menu/general.png',  -- optional: a white glyph on transparent, 64x64
    order = 1300,                                    -- built-in pages use 100..1200
    group = '#bgn.menu.group.client',                -- optional sidebar heading: '#bgn.menu.group.server' or your own
    hidden = true,                                   -- optional: not listed in the sidebar (open it with ShowPage; search still finds it)
    parent = 'modules',                              -- optional: the sidebar item shown as active while this page is open
    build = function(page)
        page:Section('Movement')
        page:Toggle('my_addon_enabled', 'Enable')
        page:Slider('my_addon_radius', 'Radius', 0, 5000, { help = 'In units.' })
        page:Button('Clear cache', 'my_addon_clear', { confirm = true, danger = true })
    end,
})
Method Notes page:Section(title, help, accent) Starts a titled card (accent = true tints it like the quick settings block); the following controls go into it. The heading appears with the first visible row. page:Toggle(cvar, label, opts) opts.on_change(enabled). page:Slider(cvar, label, min, max, opts) opts.decimals (0), opts.limit — the max for typed values (they may pass max). The value is sent on release. page:Button(label, command or function, opts) opts.text caption, opts.confirm (true or a question), opts.danger, opts.admin. page:Color(label, { r, g, b }, opts) Three integer cvars. page:Choice(cvar, label, { { value, text }, ... }, opts) Segmented control for a few string values; opts.on_change(value); opts.get() gives the active value when cvar is a console command. page:Note(text) A muted paragraph between cards. page:Row(label, help, server, cvar) An empty row: put your panel into row.control, it is placed on the right. cvar is searchable. page:Custom(function(panel) end) Any panel, docked at the top. Hidden while searching.

Search builds every page with a filter: rows that don't match are created in a hidden panel, so build functions need no changes. page.filter is set while searching (skip expensive work there if needed).

Common options: help (a '#key' label uses '#key.help' when it exists), server (default: the cvar is a bgNPC.CVars setting; hides the control from non-admins). opts.admin does the same for buttons.

Other API: bgNPC.Menu.Open(page), ShowPage(page), Close(), IsOpen(), RemovePage(id), Confirm(text, on_yes, danger), Dialog(width, build), Sound(name), colors (the current palette), Builder (add your own control methods).

docs.title: Other works
docs.text: The last page (other_works, order = math.huge, highlight = true tints it in the sidebar) shows a random page of the author's Workshop items: preview, title, short description, Subscribe (steamworks.Subscribe). The page count is read from the first page. Previews are cached in data/bgn_workshop/<id>.jpg|png; GIF previews are skipped. A failed load is not retried until the next map, the page says it couldn't load. Any page can use highlight = true.

docs.title: Interface size and migration
docs.text:
bgn_cl_ui_scale (0.75 - 2, default 1, Settings, My settings) multiplies the menu scale, which otherwise follows the screen size (Menu.Scale); the menu reopens on change.

One-time migration (systems/sh_settings_migration.lua): while bgn_settings_rev (server) / bgn_cl_settings_rev (client) is 0, the settings that 2.x turned on by itself go back to the old behavior: ghost crowd off, bgn_actor_body auto -> npc, bgn_brain auto -> fsm. A client already in bgn_mode new keeps its choice.

docs.title: First start: setup wizard
docs.text:
On the first map (5 seconds after loading, while bgn_mode_chosen is 0) the setup wizard opens with every step (the same as bgn_wizard all), only for the owner of the game (singleplayer or the listen server host). bgn_mode_chosen is set to 1 at that moment. A player who joins a server is never greeted; the wizard stays available from the menu and the console.

The wizard (ui/menu/cl_menu_wizard.lua) shows a title, a short text, a looped clip and the controls of the step. The controls are the settings rows (Menu.NewBuilder), so server rows are hidden from non-admins and a step without a visible row is skipped. Changes apply at once; closing the wizard does not roll them back.

The wizard text is written in plain words, its controls have their own short labels (bgn.wizard.<step>.*) and no technical help text (builder.nohelp), and segmented choices sit under their label (builder.stack). There is no separate mode window: the body step chooses between regular Half-Life 2 NPCs (replacers and mods for standard NPCs keep working, lightest on the PC) and NextBot (ghost crowd, GOAP, staged scenes; replacers do not affect it, heavier). The bgn_mode client setting (classic by default) is only set by bgn_classic and decides which modern steps the plain bgn_wizard hides.

Steps: crowd density, body, brain, ghost crowd, scenic scenes, wanted and arrest, voices and sound, vehicles. The body, brain and ghost crowd steps are advanced: they show up on the first start and in bgn_wizard all, not in the plain bgn_wizard. Steps with modern = true (body, brain, ghosts, scenic scenes) are skipped in Classic, except for bgn_wizard all. The vehicles step has Workshop cards: Decent Vehicle (required) and a pack of three items (simfphys, GTA SA cars, Background NPCs support) that is subscribed at once.

Command Opens bgn_wizard The wizard without the advanced steps bgn_wizard all The wizard with every step bgn_mode_chosen 0 Nothing now: the wizard comes back on the next map

The wizard can be opened from the Quick settings block and from My settings. The block is at the top of the General page until it is closed with its cross (bgn_menu_quick_hidden, a client setting), and is always at the top of the Tools page.

docs.title: Classic spawn menu pages
docs.text:
Spawn menu → Options → Background NPCs also keeps the pages of the old versions (General, Actors, Spawn, Wanted, Arrest, Extensions, Optimization, Addons, Client, Workshop) for those who are used to them. They are generated from the PAGES table in ui/settings/cl_classic_settings.lua: an item is { kind, cvar_or_command, phrase_key, ... } (check, slider, button, actors), a page marked admin = true shows a note to non-admins. Text comes from resource/localization/<lang>/bgn_*.properties (English and Russian, or the language chosen in the settings window). An item whose cvar or command no longer exists is skipped. The Settings page there opens the new window.
