Admin command bgn_classic / chat !bgn_classic applies the classic preset (bgNPC.ClassicPreset in systems/sh_classic_mode.lua, the same one the Classic mode uses).

Add a step: an entry of STEPS in cl_menu_wizard.lua (id, clip, frames, labels, modern, advanced, build(page)) and the phrases bgn.wizard.<id> and bgn.wizard.<id>.desc (plus .l1 / .l2 for the labels).

docs.title: Clips
docs.text:
GMod can't play video, so a clip is a frame atlas: materials/background_npcs/wizard/<clip>.jpg, 2048x2048, 5 columns of 384x216 frames, 45 frames played at 10 fps. With labels the first label is shown over the first half of the frames and the second over the rest ("before" / "after"). A missing atlas draws a plain placeholder.

python tools/make_wizard_clips.py <addon root> <clip> <frames dir> [<frames dir> ...] builds an atlas: every folder gives an equal share of the frames (two folders: before, after), the first two frames of each folder are dropped. The clips were recorded in game on gm_bigcity_improved: a fixed time step (host_framerate 10), a screenshot per frame, a free camera and hand-made scenes (NPCs placed in front of the camera, a staged firefight, a chase with the wanted level set).

docs.title: Crowd density
docs.text: One choice (General page for an admin, Client page for everybody else, and the first wizard step) sets bgn_max_npc (type limits follow it), bgn_ghost_crowd_max and bgn_cl_ghost_crowd_max. It works on any server, by who presses it: an admin changes the server limits and his own ghosts; a player changes only his own ghosts (bgn_cl_ghost_crowd_max), and only while the server does not run the ghost crowd (bgn_ghost_crowd 0). When the server runs the ghosts and the player is not an admin, the choice is locked with the reason. Low 25 / 0 ghosts, Medium 35 / 40 (defaults), High 60 / 80, Ultra 100 / 150. Console: bgn_crowd_density low|medium|high|ultra. No preset is selected when the limits were changed by hand. Presets: DENSITY in ui/menu/cl_menu_pages.lua.

docs.title: Setting change notices
docs.text:
Every change of a setting shows a notice in the bottom right corner, drawn above the menus: a blue SERVER plate (#03a9f4) for a server setting (also one changed by the testing mode's Fix button), announced to all players after the server has applied it, and an amber CLIENT plate (#dea909) for a bgn_cl_* setting, shown only to its player. A plate has the name and old > new; every change gets a plate (no cap, the stack grows upwards), a plate lives 6 seconds and they leave one by one in the order they came; every switch makes a new plate, while a slider changed again updates its own plate in place instead of stacking new ones, and the limits that the mod rewrites by itself after bgn_max_npc are not announced. If an admin's copy is stale, the server sends the real value back quietly.

The notices are standalone (core/sh_notice.lua): the file is included first, has its own network string, language check and drawing, and a drawing error is caught, so a failure of any later script cannot silence them. For your own cvar call bgNPC.Notice.Watch(name) (server cvar: everybody sees it; client cvar: its player).

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Actors move with the help of one navigation provider, chosen per map (bgNPC.Nav, server only).

Provider Data Used when custom own node graph, data/background_npcs/graph/<map>.dat a route file (or an old route file) exists for the map navmesh the map's NavMesh the map ships a NavMesh nodegraph the map's maps/graphs/<map>.ain no NavMesh, but the map has an HL2 node graph custom (empty) generated at runtime none of the above

The addon never starts the engine's NavMesh generation.

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
Command / cvar Meaning bgn_nav_provider auto\|navmesh\|nodegraph\|custom force a provider (auto by default) bgn_nav_info print the active provider and its size bgn_nav_reload reload navigation data bgn_nav_generate generate nodes over the whole map (flood fill from spawn points and players) bgn_nav_generate around [radius] generate only around you bgn_nav_generate stop stop the generator bgn_nav_generator_max_nodes node limit of the generator (15000) bgn_dynamic_nodes 1 keep generating around players on maps without saved data bgn_convert_legacy_nodes [map] convert an old route file (background_npcs/nodes/<map>.dat) to the new format bgn_compile pack route, seats and Decent Vehicle waypoints into a Lua file for the Workshop bgn_save_map save the active movement graph to your duplications

Save for the Workshop (bgn_compile) also downloads the route pack to the calling admin's computer: garrysmod/data/background_npcs/compile/bgn_compile_<map>.txt. A result window shows the path and explains how to rename it to .lua and put it in the published addon's lua/autorun/server folder. The pack includes the current graph, including one loaded from a duplication.

Old route files are converted automatically on load, so map packs made for older versions keep working. Unversioned routes and versions 1.0–1.2 are supported from data/citizens_points/ and data/background_npcs/nodes/ (.dat or .json). Loading leaves the original files intact. Automatic loading saves the converted route in the current format to data/background_npcs/graph/<map>.dat. A valid new graph takes precedence; a broken graph is rebuilt from a legacy route when available. Large graphs bypass JSON's 15,000-entry limits and keep their coordinates without rounding. Saved point and link counts are checked when loading; a mismatch is reported as corruption. Autocomplete for bgn_convert_legacy_nodes lists server maps with legacy routes and no new graph yet. Without an argument, the command converts the current map.

Select a route in the spawn menu's Duplications tab to load it on the server and into the point editor. Old SLibrary BGN_NODES duplications work without SLibrary. Save the route from the editor to keep it after a map restart; loading a duplication does not overwrite the saved route. Saving and loading require admin rights, and new duplications can only be loaded on their original map.

docs.title: Editing routes
docs.text: The Point editor tool edits the custom graph: create points, link them ("walk" links), remove them, then save with the panel button (cl_citizens_save_route). The Path finder tool shows the path an actor would take between two points.

docs.title: API (server)
docs.text:
bgNPC.Points.Count()
bgNPC.Points.GetInRadius(center, radius, link_type)   -- point objects with :GetPos()
bgNPC.Points.GetRandom(center, radius, link_type)
bgNPC.Points.FindPath(start_pos, end_pos, nil, link_type, actor) -- list of Vector, never empty
bgNPC.Nav.GetProvider()   -- the active provider
bgNPC.Nav.GetInfo()       -- { provider, points, links, source }

bgNPC.NodeGraph is the graph class behind the custom provider (spatial hash, typed links, A*).

Points.GetRandom returns a Vector or nil when there are no suitable points; an empty graph radius query does not fall back to another part of the map. NavMesh samples use the loaded list of areas, not a guessed continuous range of area IDs. Run bgn_nav_reload after changing the mesh externally.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hook Realm Arguments BGN_NavProviderChanged server provider BGN_NavGeneratorFinished server graph, added_count BGN_NavEditorGraphLoaded client graph BGN_PreLoadRoutes, BGN_PostLoadRoutes server OUTDATED, still called BGN_LoadingClientRoutes client OUTDATED, still called

docs.title: Emergency cars (Decent Vehicle)
docs.text: Police cars (npc_dvbgn_police) chasing an enemy, and ambulances sent to a body (actor.drive_target_pos), ignore traffic rules: siren on, no stopping at red lights or giving way. The route is the shortest one over the DV waypoints taken in both directions, with jumps to waypoints within 600 units in sight (lane changes, the opposite side of the road). When the target is in plain sight the car drives straight at it. Paths are refreshed every 3 s, every 1 s within 1000 units of the target. While an actor sits in a police car or an ambulance, players can't get in (locked sound).

docs.title: Doors
docs.text:
Cvar (server) Default Meaning bgn_npc_open_doors 1 actors open closed doors on their way; 0: only open doors are walked through bgn_npc_open_locked_doors 0 locked doors too: unlocked to open, locked again when closed after 10 s

Menu: General → Doors. bgNPC.Util.CanActorOpenDoor(door) checks both, bgNPC.Util.IsDoorOpen(door) tells an open door (prop_door_rotating, func_door*). Engine NPCs get CAP_OPEN_DOORS only while doors are allowed, NextBots open only the doors allowed; paths route only through doors that are open or may be opened. An open door is not "opened" again: the opening animation used to stop actors in the doorway. On the server, CanActorOpenDoor also rejects doors reserved by hold_door, including when opening locked doors is enabled. GOAP can close and hold an open door when desperate; police can breach that temporary hold. See door shelter and breaching.

Doorways: an actor within 90 units of a door doesn't collide with other actors (COLLISION_GROUP_NPC_SCRIPTED, actor/events/sv_door_pass.lua), so a crowd going both ways passes instead of jamming. Players and props still collide; sitting or riding actors keep their group.

docs.title: Scenic scenes
docs.text:
Staged scenes that appear on the map by themselves: a food line, a cop knocking on a door, a couple on a couch, someone sitting on a chair, an arrest at a wall. 28 scene definitions, 23 enabled for automatic spawning; all data is in config/states/sh_scenic.lua. The actors are ordinary actors (bgNPC:SpawnActor), so they work with an NPC body and with a NextBot body.

Cvar (server) Default Meaning bgn_scenic 1 scenes on / off bgn_scenic_max 4 scenes at once bgn_scenic_period 30 seconds between spawn attempts

Menu: Spawn page, section "Scenic scenes", and the Scenic scenes step of the wizard (New mode on, Classic off). Console: bgn_scenic_clear removes every scene, bgn_scenic_spawn <id> (admin) makes one near you. For door scenes, aim at a fully closed door; the command uses the same placement finder as automatic spawning. Knocking does not require a lock: both unlocked and locked doors work. The scene never locks the door; as soon as it starts opening, the actor leaves the pose and resumes normal behavior. Manual placement by an administrator allows spawning in sight and nearby, while keeping floor, room, scene placement and actor-model checks. Automatic spawning still requires hidden positions. Each automatic scene has its own checkbox on the Spawn page (also in Classic settings), backed by bgn_scenic_<id>; it affects future automatic selection, not existing scenes or manual Tool placement. sky_watch, door_brace, luggage, ration and newspaper have weight = 0 and stay manual-only. Carry previews create one walking carrier (ration/newspaper require NextBots, luggage uses a client-only briefcase on HL2 NPCs); ordinary citizens get these items through their actor config.

docs.title: Scene debugger Tool
docs.text:
Open Q → Tools → Background NPCs → Scene debugger (administrators only). The panel lists all 28 scene IDs, including five manual-only previews, plus a GOAP: hold, breach, recover test.

Control Action Left click Create the selected scene at the aimed floor/wall, fully closed door or supported free chair. Right click on an actor or temporary ragdoll Inspect the actor's UID, actual body class, state, health, model, sequence and linked door. GOAP details also print to your console. Right click on empty space Return to the last scene's summary and model/sequence failure messages. R Remove the last test created with this Tool, including actors that have already resumed normal behavior. Undo / Z Undo a Tool or bgn_scenic_spawn placement. Existing map doors/chairs are retained.

For walls, aim near the floor so the finder can find the ground; sky scenes need open sky. A rejected placement shows its reason. If a normally selected actor model lacks the animation, the HUD reports its model and requested sequences; the model is never replaced. Removing a chair test frees the chair for immediate retesting. For a door scene, aim directly at the door panel. Wrong targets, open/moving doors, and insufficient floor space have separate error messages; pointing at the floor beside a door does not select it.

The door test starts at a closed, unlocked rotating door with free space on both sides. It spawns a citizen and an officer using normal model selection and the current server body setting, gives only this pair GOAP, sets the holder to 25% health so it seeks shelter, then opens the door. The citizen closes/holds it, the officer kicks it open, and the citizen falls and recovers. The officer stops fighting after one kick. Follow the live phase/state HUD; use R or Undo to remove the pair afterwards. A model without doorbracer_* or an unreachable position is reported rather than forcing a different model or bypassing AI movement.

To compare bodies, change bgn_actor_body npc / bgn_actor_body nextbot in the normal server settings and create a new test; NextBots require a NavMesh. The Tool does not change global body/brain settings. AI around the test remains active, so use a quiet test area. Placement and diagnostics are server-authoritative; the client only selects a scene and displays the report. Tests are owned by their creator and removed on disconnect. Actors from this Tool or bgn_scenic_spawn are excluded from automatic removal/recycling and scenic distance/visibility/lifetime cleanup, even after leaving their pose. R, Undo, explicit cleanup and death still work.

docs.title: How a scene is placed
docs.text:
1. The bgn_scenic task (systems/scenic/sv_scenic_spawner.lua) picks a scene by weight, with a back-off cooldown per scene that failed to find a place (20 s doubling up to 600 s).
  2. sv_scenic_finders.lua takes seeds by the place of the scene: navigation points of the spawn ring (floor, sky, wall, ledge) or doors and chairs from an entity index cached for 30 s (door, chair).
  3. A finder checks the seed: flat floor, room for a hull, open sky above (sky), a flat wall (wall), a closed door with a clear side (door, opening/closing doors are rejected), a free chair (chair), or a wide ledge with a knee-height drop (ledge).
  4. Plan checks the floor, the level and the room of every member. Scenes keep 400 units from each other and out of sight of players (IsHiddenSpawnPosition).

docs.title: Actors
docs.text:
Members play a looped sequence in the scenic_npc state (calm group). Calm states do not pull them out; a reaction to danger (shot, hit, wanted) does, then they are normal actors again. Conversations skip them. Door scenes (door_knock, door_brace, entrance_block) also end for each participant when the linked door starts opening or is removed. The server stops the animation and returns the actor to normal AI; the actor is kept alive and is no longer removed with the scene. door_knock aligns its sideways-authored animation with the door so the raised hand reaches the panel. An automatic scene is removed after ttl seconds (default 60) once nobody watches it, even inside the spawn radius: no player is within bgn_spawn_block_radius, and none looks toward it with a clear line to the scene (a world trace). The check runs every 5 s.

Offline door placement/lifecycle checks: python tools/test_scenic.py (requires lupa).

docs.title: Adding a scene
docs.text:
Add an entry to bgNPC.cfg.scenic; the fields are described at the top of sh_scenic.lua. A model that lacks a sequence plays the next one of the list; a scene whose sequences no model has is skipped. Models, skins and bodygroups come from ordinary actor spawning, including actor config and model hooks. Scenes do not override models (members.models is ignored); participants without a supported sequence are skipped instead of being given a different model. An atomic = true scene (the couch pair) is cancelled as a whole if either participant lacks a usable pose. Set weight = 0 to keep a scene manual-only.

Not ported: scenes with custom sounds, rappel, APC, binoculars and characters of the original addon.

docs.title: Placement and pose rules
docs.text:
Both couches and the radio desk are automatic again, with indoors = true. Placement requires a solid ceiling within 384 units and walls in all four horizontal directions within 512 units, plus a dry flat floor. Sky ceilings, open courtyards and furniture whose rotated bounds intersect brush geometry are rejected. This conservative check can reject a real room with an open doorway/window; it also applies to the Tool.

ground_sit creates one citizen with a supported pose selected from a list. Plain standing scenes (plaza, tired) were removed: their poses (plazastand*, idle_subtle, d2_coast03_postbattle_idle02) now belong to the idle state. The raised-arm tired pose is tired_wall, facing its support. ledge_sitting needs a flat lip at least 32 units wide, 28 units of support behind it, clear standing room, and a 24–56 unit drop in front. Short downward traces also require support directly below the pelvis and 10 units to either side; the actor faces the lower surface. Thin rails, ordinary stair steps and deep falls are rejected. Seated NextBots temporarily stop locomotion and disable the solid mask and gravity, preventing physics from lifting them above a chair, custom bench seat or ledge. Stopping the body clears both desired speed and velocity; leaving the scene restores the original mask and gravity.

Member pos.z and per-sequence seq_offsets are retained; spawning uses a separate safe standing position. Leaving the pose restores that standing position, so below-origin seated animations do not strand the actor in the floor or ledge. Couch seating uses one calibrated furniture model; normal actor model selection is retained.

docs.title: Core engineering audit regressions
docs.text:
python tools/test_core_audit.py runs 21 isolated LuaJIT/lupa tests from tests/sv_engineering_audit.lua; SERVER bgn_selftest loads the same file on demand without live entities. The cases cover scheduler mutations, recurring services, mechanics, UID/snapshot reloads, client retirement, malformed/chunked network input, navigation, GOAP, appearance and gamemode spawn permission/accounting, regeneration, spawnmenu IO, string UID LOD and client seat downloads. Follow-up cases cover forced exit, blocked exits and lethal damage without the DV visual, plus wanted observers awaiting a replacement entity. Recheck cases cover missing bodies in regeneration, voices, relationships and scan budget yields. All 21 fail against the starting dev with --baseline and pass after these changes. This models engine calls; it is not a native game result. See audit decisions and remaining limits.

For interactive scenic and GOAP door checks, use the admin Scene debugger Tool. tools/scenic_tool.lua exercises the real server Tool, native Undo, chair cleanup, model diagnostics and the one-cycle door test on both NPC and NextBot bodies through a temporary single-player bridge. Use an isolated gm_bigcity_improved lab with a NavMesh. Report: data/bgn_scenic_tool_lab/tool.json. Keep actor-remover and scenic maintenance tasks running: the cleanup cases verify that owned tests survive while an ordinary control actor is removed with bgn_enable 0; the fixture restores that setting afterwards.

tools/door_hold.lua is an opt-in fixture for an isolated single-player gm_bigcity_improved session through a temporary Lua bridge, not an addon autorun. It tests actual GOAP holding/breaching with all four NPC/NextBot body pairings and four door headings, physical knockback, stable actor/entity/health, restored door settings, blocked stand-up, forced-state rejection, holder/ragdoll removal and damage/death while down. Report: data/bgn_door_lab/doors.json. It creates stock test rigs and doors, briefly moves the observer, pauses automatic spawners and cleans up its objects/restores tasks and observer afterward. Run it in a lab, not an ongoing play session. tools/seating_lab.lua checks 32 seating cases on both bodies: two stock chair props at four headings, close and distant approach, BigCity custom bench seats, scenic chairs/benches and both ledge poses on male and female rigs. It checks direct pelvis support, facing the drop, stable placement and physics/seat restoration on exit. Run only in an isolated SP lab on port 27025; report: data/bgn_seat_lab/seating.json.

Additional opt-in fixtures through the same temporary SP bridge:

Fixture Native checks Report under data/bgn_scenic_overhaul_lab/ tools/scenic_poses.lua NPC/NextBot poses, wall/door contact, indoor rejection, both couch sexes, complete pairs and brush ledges poses.json tools/carry_items.lua Tool/ordinary spawns: HL2 briefcase without a weapon/activity override, NextBot ration/suitcase/newspaper walk, hidden parcel, stowing, drop/expiry carry.json tools/ghost_carry.lua Run SERVER and CLIENT separately: empty hands in both ghost modes and NPC/NextBot materialization without carried items ghost-server.json, ghost-client.json tools/ragdoll_identity.lua Same actor/entity, latest health/max health, weapon/clip, incoming/outgoing relationships and wanted record after recovery identity.json

Fixtures use stock animation rigs for repeatability, clean up their own entities and restore changed settings. They do not establish support for every custom model or multiplayer behavior. scenic_poses uses real BSP geometry for its ledge test; it does not replace engine traces with stub results. tools/carry_alignment.lua is an opt-in CLIENT render-frame check in an isolated SP lab. It measures the newspaper lower grip against the fingertips, the 15-degree outward tilt and the upright briefcase handle against the index-finger grip. Inspect front and side screenshots for male/female rigs at idle and during actual walking; measurements do not replace the visual check. Reports: data/bgn_paper_lab/alignment-idle.json and alignment-walk.json.

Offline checks (lupa): python tools/test_regressions.py, python tools/test_scenic.py, python tools/test_carry_items.py.

A one-minute check that answers "nothing spawns" and "I'm an admin but can't change the settings" with facts. Open Settings → Tools → Testing (admins) or type a console command:

Command Who What it does bgn_test admins The full test (below). bgn_test_settings anyone Only the rights and settings checks. Run it first when settings won't change. bgn_test_report anyone Opens the results of the last test again. bgn_test_stop the player who started it, admins Stops a running test.

docs.title: What the full test checks
docs.text:
Check How Addon and map bgn_enable, navigation provider and points. Admin rights What the server and the client think of your group (IsAdmin, IsSuperAdmin, user group). Changing server settings The client sets the test cvar bgn_test_server_value the same way every settings row does, the server must receive it; then the server changes it itself and the client must see it. Changing client settings The test cvar bgn_cl_test_value is set and read back. Actors spawn on their own Actors exist or the regular spawner creates one within 15 s. If not, the most likely reason is named: addon off, zero limits, no navigation points, no spot out of sight, other addon. Actors spawn on demand One actor of each active type is created at free spots around you, ignoring limits and visibility rules. Wanted-only types are skipped. Cars Decent Vehicle is loaded, the map has its waypoints, the configured car models are installed; a driver is spawned with a car and has to get in. Missing Decent Vehicle is a warning, not an error. Actors don't vanish The spawned actors and cars must still exist 12 s later. An actor spawned over its type limit is expected to be removed (the log says so). Actor states Every actor has a valid entity and a known state, stands inside the world, walkers really move, and a forced idle / walk change is accepted. Where the actors are Actors closer than 700 units form a group. The camera flies over the four biggest ones, outlining the actors and marking the spot with a beam and a sphere. Space skips it. You are frozen and invulnerable meanwhile.

Test actors and cars are removed at the end, the changed cvars are restored.

docs.title: The Fix button
docs.text: Where the cause is obvious and the cure is a setting, an admin sees Fix on the row: the addon switched off, a zero total limit, all actor types off, a spawn radius with no points in it, block and visibility radii that leave no free spot, car support off. It restores the default values of just those console variables (the log lists them) and asks to run the test again. Rights, missing addons and maps without navigation have no button: they can't be fixed from a setting.

docs.title: Results window
docs.text:
It has the settings window's look, the same light / dark switch, and one row per check with an icon (passed, warning, failed) and a short plain sentence. Copy log puts the full technical report into the clipboard (it is also saved to data/background_npcs/test_report.txt); the server console prints it too. Paste it into a bug report. The sentences follow the interface language; the log is always English.

================================================================
 Background NPCs - test report
================================================================
 Version  : 2.0.1
 Map      : gm_construct
 Server   : listen server, 2 player(s)
 Result   : 8 passed, 1 warnings, 1 failed
================================================================

[FAIL] Admin rights
       The server does not see you as an admin (your group: user). ...
       | server: IsAdmin=false IsSuperAdmin=false group="user" listen host=false
       | client: IsAdmin=false IsSuperAdmin=false group="user"

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• In single player and on a listen server the client and the server share console variables, so the server settings check can pass without admin rights; it then ends with a warning. Run it on the real server.
  • Only admins can run the full test; for others bgn_test runs the settings checks only.
  • The two test cvars are also sliders in Tools → Testing: change them by hand to see what a normal row does.
  • Source: lua/background_npcs_core/debug/ (sv_diag.lua runs the checks, cl_diag.lua is the camera and the window). A check is a function that calls Section(id), Log(...) and Result(status, phrase, ...); phrases live in resource/localization/<lang>/bgn_diag.properties.

docs.title: Actor overlay and regression checks
docs.text: Debugging is admin-only and requires bgn_debug 1 (SERVER). CLIENT controls affect only the viewer. Inspection records existing decisions; it does not run sensors, roll reactions, advance plans or change stealth rules.

docs.title: Spawnmenu debug page
docs.text:
Open Q → Options → Background NPCs → Debugging, or Tools → Background NPCs: Debugging → Actor inspector. Choose an actor from the refreshed list or under the crosshair. Selection uses the actor UID, including across body replacement. Pinning prevents the inspector Tool's LMB from replacing it; an explicit menu selection still works. The default is one actor and its connections. Nearby overview is optional.

Tools → Background NPCs: Editor contains route points, spawn areas and seats. Background NPCs: Debugging contains actor inspection, navigation test, actor movement, scenes and carried items. Existing Tool IDs are preserved; the internal actor spawner remains hidden.

CLIENT cvar Default Meaning bgn_cl_debug_mode 0 0: screen HUD; 1: world cards (3D2D); 2: geometry only. bgn_cl_debug_inspector 1 Screen HUD of the selected actor. bgn_cl_debug_bounds / bgn_cl_debug_labels 1 / 1 Bounds / world-card text. bgn_cl_debug_summary 1 Collection/render CPU time and geometry count in the HUD footer. bgn_cl_draw_npc_path 0 Selected actor's existing SERVER path. bgn_cl_debug_targets 1 Known-enemy connections; these are memory, not current visibility. bgn_cl_debug_vision 0 Recorded gameplay sight checks and blockers. bgn_cl_debug_signals / bgn_cl_debug_history 1 / 1 Team signals / recent events. bgn_cl_debug_text_scale 1 Text scale 0.75–2; also scales with screen height, 20 px at 900p. bgn_cl_debug_distance / bgn_cl_debug_geometry_distance 800 / 1500 Independent text / geometry limits in HU, each 100–5000. bgn_cl_debug_wh / bgn_cl_debug_overview 0 / 0 Geometry through walls / nearby actor overview. bgn_cl_debug_related / bgn_cl_debug_cards 16 / 8 Relation limit 1–64 per list / visible-card limit 1–16. bgn_cl_debug_rate 5 Selected snapshot rate, 2–10 Hz. bgn_cl_debug_seconds / bgn_cl_debug_life 30 / 2 History window 1–30 s / line lifetime 0.2–10 s. bgn_cl_debug_blockers / bgn_cl_debug_markers 1 / 1 Sight blockers / scene and hand markers. bgn_cl_debug_marker_size 12 Marker size 2–48 HU. bgn_cl_debug_team_filter, type_filter, state_filter, event_filter empty Plain substring filters; all four names have the bgn_cl_debug_ prefix. Event filter matches the event kind. bgn_cl_debug_freeze / bgn_cl_debug_technical 0 / 0 Freeze diagnostic data / show technical HUD identifiers.

Less frequent settings are in Limits and filters. World cards use distance scaling and overlap suppression; text wraps, and long reports offer copyable details. List refresh preserves selection and camera. Freeze holds the displayed snapshot, not the game or the live camera.

The compact HUD shows health, state, reaction, known enemies/targets, wanted status, movement, sight and recent events. Open details adds raw state/group, fight avoidance, model/animation, carry item, reaction weights, known-target last-seen times and the current cached GOAP plan/facts. FSM actors have no GOAP plan. A weighted reaction pick is a candidate, not proof that a later hook allowed that reaction. Attempted damage is recorded before cancellation; the reaction event does not establish actual health loss.

Sight comes from the real HasLineOfSight / CanSeeEntity calls. Channels identify damage witnesses, shot witnesses, enemy memory, ally sharing, help, wanted detection and squads. Green is a successful check, red a failed check with its hit point and blocker (including map geometry), purple is remembered enemy knowledge, yellow is a signal. Rejected signals are red. Absence of a check means unknown. The view cone is drawn only after an actual direction test, using its recorded aim vector and the same dot-product threshold as Util.IsInView; its 100 HU length is illustrative. Plain LOS has no facing restriction. A remembered enemy can be currently unseen. Wanted proximity and radio broadcasts do not imply a successful sight trace. No debugger-generated observer ray is added.

Team events identify sender → recipient and the target being discussed. Help, sharing, radio and squad handoffs record resulting enemy membership; witness-reaction vetoes are recorded separately. The wanted broadcast has no actor sender. This is a bounded journal of instrumented paths, not a complete log of every rejected AI branch.

SERVER collects selected snapshots at the requested rate and shares collection work for matching subscriptions within a tick. The actor list is requested on demand (throttled to 1 Hz); overview updates at 2 Hz within 5000 HU. There is no automatic all-actor stream. Per observed UID: at most 256 events and 64 recent sight records; paths are capped at 256 points, rosters at 128 actors, and client geometry at 1024 segments. Truncation is reported. CLIENT builds text and a colored line mesh on snapshot/settings changes, then draws the cached batch each frame; scene/hand markers refresh at 2 Hz. No per-frame actor search or diagnostic visibility traces are used. The HUD costs measure collection and client render code, not whole-frame performance or network transmission.

Toggle actor first-person view follows the selected actor's eyes. F6, Escape or Return to your view exits. SERVER adds this camera to the admin's PVS and blocks movement/attacks. The player's body remains vulnerable. Death/removal, viewer death, lost rights, map cleanup, debug disable or lost subscription releases the camera. Heartbeats are every second, expiry is 3 s, and unfrozen geometry older than 2 s stops drawing. SERVER supplies the body-relative eye frame for NPCs/NextBots; CLIENT follows body interpolation. Only the viewed body's model renderer is temporarily suppressed and restored on exit; server NoDraw is preserved.

Tool-specific checks:

  • bgn_path_finder: LMB start, RMB destination, R clear. Uses the active SERVER navigation provider; endpoint markers and point count describe this requested path, separately from an actor's current path.
  • bgn_actor_mover: LMB actor, RMB destination, R/holster release. Walk/run and arrival tolerance are configurable. One owner controls the actor; previous debugger/eternal/lock flags and state data are restored on release. This Tool deliberately changes movement; it is not passive inspection.
  • bgn_scenic_debug: existing placement, inspection, GOAP-door test and owned cleanup/Undo remain. The preview reuses placement checks, shows participant bounds and rejection reasons, and creates nothing. It uses the minimum group layout without RNG; actual spawning may choose another size/orientation/model variant.
  • bgn_carry_debug: existing give/remove checks remain. Bone axes, prop bounds, model/animation compatibility and briefcase handle-to-finger distance help inspect attachment; the number is geometric, not a rig-quality score. Both special Tools share distance, WH, marker-size controls and copyable reports.

Console equivalents: bgn_debug_select [uid], bgn_debug_details, bgn_debug_tool_details, bgn_debug_watch, bgn_debug_watch_stop, bgn_debug_clear, bgn_debug_pin, bgn_debug_freeze.

python tools/test_actor_debug.py (lupa) checks permission/payload gates, read-only snapshots, bounded history, map blockers, recorded view direction, camera lifecycle, EN/RU keys and mover restoration. Native single-player verification on gm_bigcity_improved (1280×720, 1600×900, 1920×1080) covers menu categories, real damage/sight/blockers and team handoff, HUD/3D2D distance, NPC/NextBot camera, refresh/freeze, scene preview/owned removal, carry issuance/removal and cached mesh construction. Timing samples with 30/60/100 actors cover selected inspection and optional overview; they are not a general FPS guarantee. Multiplayer and arbitrary camera addons/custom rigs still need separate verification.

python tools/test_regressions.py (requires lupa) checks the Lua logic outside GMod. It covers safe actor health accessors in both realms, arrest module registration order, seated damage and police witnesses, passenger aim, exit placement by seat/model attachment, overlap rejection and blocked-side fallback. These checks do not verify live physics or every vehicle model.

docs.title: Room siege developer checks
docs.text:
bgn_selftest includes tests/sv_siege.lua: isolated checks for one-exit pockets, alternative/incoming connections, outdoor rejection, animation/class requirements, door chance/fallback, shared deployment reservations, grenade clearance and the wait/cooldown. These do not establish real physics or map completeness.

tools/siege.lua is an opt-in SERVER fixture for an isolated single-player gm_bigcity_improved session, using the room near setpos -748.617798 -4298.178223 -11071.968750. It creates eight actors and exercises metropolice/combine operators with NPC and NextBot bodies, including a player target. It checks the double-leaf exit, missing-animation rejection, five front/three rear participants, silent waiting, one real projectile, entry into the room, actual damage/attribution against NPC targets, exit/damage cancellation and NPC capability restoration. It temporarily moves/arms the observer, pauses population tasks and cleans up/restores its own state. Run it through a temporary local SERVER bridge, never as an autorun or on a public server. Results: garrysmod/data/bgn_siege_lab/verification.json.

docs.title: DV traffic developer checks
docs.text:
Only BGN-created vehicles (isBgnVehicle) use the new recovery controller; the original DV remains a dependency. Police designation (bgnPoliceVehicle) persists across driver/group changes. Only actors on team police can drive or ride in these cars. Players may still take an empty police car.

Pedestrians keep their detour side and intermediate goals. The 30% chance of ignoring road caution does not disable navigation around solid obstacles. Local traffic scans run at most twice per second, excluding dormant actors.

Stalled drivers wait and honk before planning a bounded forward/reverse maneuver, including the opposite lane or sidewalk when space and ground support permit. Planning uses the shared task budget; control updates remain frequent. Red lights, scheduled stops and taxi passenger waits suppress recovery. Impossible maneuvers fall back to waiting and existing unseen-vehicle cleanup (bgn_vehicle_cleanup_time, default 120 seconds).

The tools/dv_*.lua fixtures use a temporary single-player file bridge on gm_bigcity_improved. The bridge is not shipped as an addon autorun. python tools/dv_lab.py server <fixture.lua> sends a fixture to the running game. Reports go to garrysmod/data/bgn_dv_lab/.

Fixtures cover police access (dv_stage1), chassis/axle alignment (dv_headings), NPC/NextBot detours (dv_stage2), blockers/turns and original-DV comparison (dv_stage3), scheduled-stop/no-path guards (dv_guards), two-way traffic (dv_duel), and stationary 10/30/60-car sensor benchmarks (dv_benchmark). Run one fixture at a time in a test session: they create entities and move the observer. Benchmark ticks_per_second measures server ticks, not rendering FPS. Python checks: python tools/test_regressions.py (requires lupa).

Local vehicle planning targets mostly level streets. Other axle layouts and steep ramps need separate calibration.

Police dismount for nearby actual enemies or critical vehicle damage; neutral observers no longer trigger dismounts or prevent returning. Previous crew may return to free passenger seats after their driver boards. dv_return_lane.lua exercises normal police return and physical alternate-lane recovery in an isolated lab. After two failed plans/maneuvers, idle traffic tries up to three nearby directed road segments with a different heading, respecting DV groups, road height, swept body clearance, ground support and reservations. A completed maneuver hands the driver to the new DV segment. Active destination missions and chases keep their routes. Progress during an alternate-lane maneuver means approaching its next target, not merely moving away from the jam.

Alternate-lane tracking uses the measured rear axle for four-wheel simfphys cars, brakes and replans from the physical pose at gear changes, and skips failed lane endpoints for 30 seconds. Its bounded search allows 640 nodes; normal recovery keeps 160 nodes and its original body-center tracking. Lane endpoints must be ahead along their own directed segment. Critically damaged police cars are not boarded again. The fixture records the exact native waypoint handover; polling PrevWaypoint alone can miss it when DV immediately advances another waypoint. BGNReturnLaneOnly=true runs only the lane portion.

Keep DV's native DoTrace interval: clear traces renew StopByTrace for only 0.1 seconds, so a 0.2-second scan interval causes false braking. Recovery requires speed below 25 HU/s and an obstacle or a heading error over 60 degrees; it refreshes DV traces while maneuvering and releases control when the forward route clears. Failed maneuvers restart the normal waiting period. Actor speed overrides retain DV's corner and traffic slowdown coefficients; absolute limits remain in HU/s.

dv_damage_horn.lua checks quiet waiting on an empty road, short honks (0.15 s, 8–14 s between requests) at a real blocker, surviving exits and fatal NPC/NextBot hits leaving ragdolls. Report: damage_horn.json. Honking requires a nearly stationary car and an entity hit by the forward sensor; world geometry does not trigger it. Exit floors more than 96 units above or below the car origin are rejected, keeping passengers aboard rather than placing them on another road level. Fatal seated occupants leave debris ragdolls subject to the engine's ragdoll limit.

Vehicle occupants keep the same actor object and UID in the population registry. Boarding removes the real NPC/NextBot and its weapons; the existing DV driver/passenger anim entity represents the occupant. Exiting recreates the original body kind, appearance, health and equipment at a free hull-tested position. A blocked exit retains the seat. Removing a car removes its crew, including direct entity removal. Addon-private NPC data requires a BGN_ActorEntityChanged(actor, old, new) integration.

dv_lifecycle.lua checks simultaneous boarding, NPC/NextBot removal and recreation, stable identities/counts/targets, health/equipment, blocked exits, repeat boarding and direct car removal. dv_lifecycle_guards.lua checks lost/failed controllers, full seats, wanted/kill history and provider cleanup. Reports: lifecycle.json and lifecycle_guards.json. Both scenarios clean up their test entities.

The admin Carried item debugger (bgn_carry_debug) issues a selected briefcase, parcel or newspaper with LMB and removes it with RMB. Aim at a living unarmed actor on foot in a calm state; model/body compatibility remains enforced. Test briefcases on male/female NPCs and NextBots through calm actions, running and combat: no physical briefcase should spawn.

Carried visual models now move with their parent entity instead of keeping a separate world render origin, so a briefcase or newspaper does not remain culled at its old location after an actor teleport.

bgn_selftest also runs tests/sv_conflicts.lua: isolated modules/hooks cover initiator direction/reset/rebind/forgetting, confirmed arrest initiation, attacker visibility, caller-visible help, foreign hostility, distinct arrest victims, strict health/distance boundaries, refusal and shared player/actor wanted thresholds. They create no live entities and do not establish engine hook timing, traces or vehicle physics.

tests/sv_pursuit.lua checks stable/direct-attacker/group target priorities, observation of every enemy, original shared timestamps, hidden-target approach without standoff, visible-only cover, hidden squad columns, and the inclusive combat-radius boundary. Native integration also needs ordinary non-eternal actors with the remover enabled: observe a target through an open door, close it, then add reinforcements without manually seeding their memory. Verify pursuit/siege and no recycling inside the radius, then removal after leaving it; exercise NextBot unstuck protection separately.

docs.title: Combat audit regressions
docs.text:
bgn_selftest loads these SERVER tests on demand, without creating live entities:

File Interaction checked tests/sv_pursuit.lua Real NPC adapter with modelled engine-memory refresh: search expires after more than 60 s and actual sightings renew it; real Rebind transfers hidden position/time and priorities in both realm branches; equipment follows the selected enemy with arrest fallback; both real NextBot teleport methods reject combat at 1000 and allow it at 1000.1, retaining siege protection. tests/sv_siege.lua Negotiation's hold_fire rejects both siege initiation and follower recruitment. tests/sv_negotiation.lua Weapon capabilities are removed and restored while door capabilities survive. tests/sv_conflicts.lua Friendly manhack damage is blocked in both owner/reaction hook orders, including ownership available only through inflictor; invalid owners are not substituted.

An external LuaJIT/lupa run passed 36 tests across conflicts, lethal weapons, negotiation, pursuit, siege and GOAP planning after the fixes. The six affected checks failed against the earlier implementation. The external harness models engine APIs and is not a native bgn_selftest run. Native multiplayer, vehicle/door physics, real engine memory timing and script reload during these actions still require separate verification.

tests/sv_team_damage.lua runs 10 isolated regressions with real team, enemy, damage, wanted, arrest and vehicle-reaction modules: friendly NPC/NextBot hits with team damage off/on; help/report rejection; wanted broadcast and stale-entry cleanup; ordinary kills; SetTeam/AddTeam cleanup; repeated ramming of police on foot or in a car and a pedestrian run-over keep the driver in residents. tools/test_police_force.py also verifies a distant friendly hit is not a ranged threat. These are modelled engine calls, not native physics evidence.

docs.title: Vehicles and Decent Vehicle
docs.text: DV is optional. Install Decent Vehicle, the car content used by your actor config, and DV waypoints for the map. Pedestrian navigation and DV roads are separate. Server providers own boarding and driving; clients render seated actors.

docs.title: Character identity and damage
docs.text:
Boarding preserves Actor/UID but replaces its entity; exit restores the saved body at a free seat-specific position. A blocked exit keeps the actor aboard. Use actor health accessors and BGN_ActorEntityChanged for integrations. SERVER also preserves the registered Actor/UID during forced ejection when another actor seizes a car, so the restored body continues its normal AI instead of becoming an orphan. SERVER also gives an actor that steps out of a moving car 3 seconds of immunity to damage from that same car.

On SERVER, a living seated Actor may temporarily outlive its DV visual entity. Removing that entity attempts a forced exit using the chassis position/orientation when seat data is unavailable; stored health and Actor/UID survive a successful exit. If no safe exit exists, the removal handler retires the actor. Vehicle cleanup never restores bodies. Lethal damage can still place a corpse beside a valid car after its occupant visual has gone.

docs.title: Driving and verification
docs.text:
Emergency routing, traffic recovery and developer fixtures, arrest in a car.

Police keep pursuing driving suspects, use ranged weapons against enemies in cars and avoid boarding loops. An officer steps out when a live enemy is within 800 units of the car and is not driving away (its car moved within the last 6 s), or the car is at 20% health or less. A seated officer has no NPC senses: once a second the server makes a hostile NPC (hostile to players) or a NextBot hunting a player/actor within 1000 units and in sight of the car its enemy, unless bgn_ignore_another_npc is on. Siren control has one owner and tolerates brief target loss. Native DV sensor timing is preserved; bounded local recovery handles blocked vehicles without replacing DV globally. Vehicle spawn distance and hidden cleanup have separate settings from pedestrians.

Steep ramps and unusual axle layouts require separate live calibration. Stub regressions do not prove every vehicle model or map.

Cars farther than 1500 units from every player (3500 when in view) and not in a chase, recovery or flight think every 0.05 s, scan every 0.25 s and do not start recovery planning (bgn_vehicle_lod, default 1; modules/dv/sv_vehicle_lod.lua). They return to native timing as soon as a player comes near. In a 12-car test this cut DV think time from 151 to 96 ms/s.

Friendly police hits do not activate the seated-driver execution timer. Friendly hits do not force occupants to exit or turn a citizen into an offender. Vehicle collisions do not remove civilian team protection either: running over a civilian or ramming police keeps the driver allied (wanted).

docs.title: Voices
docs.text: NPC phrases are voiced (XTTS-v2, generated): citizens (calm, fear, the 911 call after the operator answers; a male and a female take), the police (combat shouts, arrest orders, detention, squad formation calls, siege and hostage-negotiation radio calls, a downed or lost target, wounded falling back, officer down, luggage warnings, reporting and writing down a body, confiscating a car), gangsters (carjacking) and every conversation line. English and Russian; the police speak through a radio filter.

docs.title: Who plays what
docs.text:
The setting is per player (client only). The server never plays a voice clip: it only tells every client who says which line, and each client plays it in its own language, or not at all.

Cvar (client) Default Meaning bgn_cl_voices 1 1 voiced, 0 silent; the same conversation clips in both actor modes bgn_cl_voice_language auto language of the NPC phrases and voices: auto (the game language), english, russian

Settings window: My settings. The server's bgn_module_replics_language still forces one phrase language for everyone when it is not auto.

The police combat shouts (police_combat, police_contact) fire on every hit and every entry into combat, so Actor:Voice lets one of them through per officer every 20 s (COMBAT_VOICE_COOLDOWN in actor/components/sh_speech.lua). Other lines (arrest, officer down, body report) have no cooldown.

Text over the head (actor/cl_actor_text_say.lua): a dark plate with the speaker's name in the team color (police blue, medics green, bandits orange, zombies yellow-green, others grey), an accent bar and the line wrapped by words. It rises and fades in, fades out at the end and from 600 to 800 units away.

docs.title: Lines
docs.text:
Phrases live in lua/background_npcs_core/config/replics/language/sh_<language>.lua (bgNPC.cfg.replics[id]). A clip is

sound/background_npcs/vo/<language>/<id>/<index>[_f].ogg

index is the phrase's place in its table, _f the female take (picked by the model's file name: female / woman / women first, then male / man / men). So the voice-only tables (police_*, gangster_*, stare_*, brawl_*, call_911) and conversation tables (conv_*) must have the same number of lines, in the same order, in every language.

-- text over the head + voice (the index must exist in the English table, the server's)
actor:SayReplic('fear', 3)
-- voice only: each client picks a line; the event sound is a fallback if the clip is missing
actor:Voice('police_arrest_order', 'npc/metropolice/vo/getdown.wav')
-- event sound only (also muted by bgn_cl_voices 0)
actor:Voice(nil, 'npc/metropolice/vo/defender.wav')

docs.title: Generating clips
docs.text:
tools/make_voices.py (not shipped) reads the language files and config/states/sh_conversations.lua and voices only new or changed lines (tools/voices_state.json); clips of removed lines are deleted. In a conversation every participant keeps one voice. It uses the XTTS worker and dxRevive of the mlp-g5 pipeline (D:/mlp-g5-work/pipeline/scripts/voice_tts.py, read-only: nothing there is changed).

D:/mlp-g5-work/tools/tts_venv/Scripts/python tools/make_voices.py [--force] [--only <line id>]

Mono Ogg Vorbis, 44.1 kHz, about 20 KB a clip.

docs.title: Wanted levels and offenders
docs.text:
Sources: systems/wanted/, config/states/sh_wanted.lua. The server owns wanted state and reactions; clients receive records and render the HUD/halos.

Server cvar Default Purpose bgn_enable_wanted_mode 1 Enables wanted behavior; changing it clears existing wanted entries. bgn_wanted_time 30 Base wanted duration in seconds. bgn_wanted_level 1 Allows level escalation (up to level 5). bgn_wanted_level_up_period 60 Seconds between automatic level-ups of a wanted NPC/actor (never a player); needs bgn_wanted_level; 0 disables. bgn_wanted_police_instantly 1 Enables immediate police response handling. bgn_wanted_impunity_limit 5 Impunity threshold used by wanted actions. bgn_wanted_impunity_reduction_period 10 Seconds between impunity reductions.

Kills, witnesses, police calls and arrest refusal feed wanted handling. Ignored/arrested players and resident/medic actors are excluded from new wanted entries. Actor wanted identity survives DV body replacement. While any resident is within 600 units of the target or sees it within bgn_wanted_detection_radius, the timer is reset every second and does not run, for players and actors alike; a car the target sits in counts as the target for the sight check. A non-player wanted target that stays 15 seconds outside every player's field of view, or farther than half of bgn_spawn_radius_visibility (obstacles are not checked), is dropped; this is separate from player wanted expiry and population removal.

Residents and police sharing a team cannot become enemies through an ordinary hit or kill. Friendly hits do not start fear, help, arrest or crime reporting; bgn_team_damage controls health damage only. AddWanted rejects resident actors, and regular cleanup removes stale resident entries. SetTeam/AddTeam reconcile mutual enemy lists immediately; becoming a resident clears wanted, and joining the primary officer's team clears that actor's arrest.

Nothing in the addon removes a civilian's residents team. Vehicle collisions are no exception: running over a civilian or ramming an officer or a police car never turns the driver into an offender. Police in a car ignore a civilian driver's ram and take no damage from it; a ram by a non-civilian actor keeps the 10% reaction chance. See brains and arrest.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
SERVER detection requires both a living Actor and a valid current entity. A seated observer awaiting body replacement cannot refresh the wanted timer until its entity is restored; Actor:IsAlive() alone does not guarantee an engine entity exists.

Obtain local wanted = bgNPC.Modules.Get('wanted') after systems load; it may be nil before then or in a different realm. Query wanted:HasWanted(entity), GetWanted(entity) and GetAllWanted(). Change state on SERVER with AddWanted(entity, time) and RemoveWanted(entity); adding an existing target does not reset or extend its timer. AddWanted returns nil for a protected resident/medic actor. The returned wanted record supports UpdateWanted(time), SetLevel(level), LevelUp() and LevelDown(); nonpositive SetLevel removes wanted, levels above 5 are capped.

Hooks include BGN_AddWantedTarget, BGN_RemoveWantedTarget, BGN_WantedLevelUp, BGN_WantedLevelDown. The server sends existing records to a player on BGN_PlayerReady. Client UI options do not disable the authoritative server system.

docs.title: Conflict memory and witnesses
docs.text:
SERVER keeps one directed record per pair in the existing first_attacker module. Only confirmed positive damage creates a record; vehicles resolve to their driver. Retaliation refreshes the timestamp without reversing the initiator. A defender can still initiate a separate conflict against someone else. Same-team actors and the existing consensual brawl are excluded. Residents/police do not blame a retaliating victim unless it is already a threat to their team. A player attacking a foreign NPC/NextBot with Disposition(player) == D_HT is defending against that entity; missing Disposition is safe.

Before blaming an initiator, every actor applies the common-enemy rule: if the damaged target is already in that observer's enemy list, the hit does not make its attacker an enemy. This exception is refused when observer and attacker already list one another as enemies in either direction, or there is D_HT between observer and attacker in either direction (configured relationships, body dispositions and available entity Disposition methods). It creates no permanent alliance and clears no enemy entries. For example, a neutral gangster shooting a player already hunted by police is not blamed for the first hit, even without wanted status. Factual pair initiator memory is still kept; a later attack on an uninvolved ally is a separate offense. IsEnemyOfTeam includes the observer's own enemy list as well as its teammates.

Damage witnesses must see the attacker within 2500 units, with LOS and, for attacking actors, FOV. Seeing only the victim or knowing wanted status does not bypass this. Other teams protect their allies; residents/police also resolve conflicts between outsiders. Enemy assignment and wanted status are separate. CallForHelp shares a threat with teammates within 1000 units who see the caller, without requiring enemy visibility or FOV; periodic sharing keeps its existing team/gang rules.

Records expire after 60 seconds without damage or LOS between the participants (either direction, no FOV). Death, completed arrest and wanted removal clear every record involving that entity in either role. DV body replacement transfers both roles and the impunity counter. This memory is server-only, not a client snapshot.

docs.title: Initial wanted assignment
docs.text:
With wanted enabled and peaceful mode off, players and actors not currently in residents share the main kill handler's witnessed-kill impunity threshold (>= bgn_wanted_impunity_limit, 0 disables), reduced by one each bgn_wanted_impunity_reduction_period seconds (0 disables decay). Counts concern killed actors. Instant wanted for killing a police actor additionally requires another living police actor to see the killer with LOS and FOV within 2500 units; the dying officer and killer cannot be witnesses. Ordinary threshold kills also require a witness with LOS/FOV.

A foreign entity (neither player nor actor) becomes wanted without a witness if it kills any residents/police actor, or has Disposition(actor) == D_HT towards any living residents/police actor. Hostility is polled once per second; bgn_ignore_another_npc disables this polling. For local enemy detection, a hostile foreign entity must be within 2500 units and LOS; FOV is not required. Foreign NPC dispositions towards ordinary actor bodies are preserved instead of being replaced from player relations; the existing NextBot player-disposition adapter remains in use. There is no guessed hostility for entities without Disposition.

Completed witness calls and police radio backup remain wanted sources. Resident/medic and existing ignored/arrested exclusions remain protected. Arrest escalation is described on the arrest page. Wanted assignment still informs all police immediately.

docs.title: Behavior decision tree
docs.text:
The optional held-weapon reaction is a separate SERVER input, without damage:

Actor killed → inspect last damage and the killer's current active weapon
├─ Explosion / vehicle damage / player killing from a vehicle → do not learn
└─ Same attacker + valid active weapon + new class → cache it, rewrite DATA (even with checkbox off)

Once per second: bgn_react_to_lethal_weapon = 1, non-peaceful mode
├─ Living player/NPC/NextBot holds a class from the cache
└─ Living residents/police observer; not self, teammate or existing enemy
   ├─ Ignored player / player in friend mode / beyond 800 / outside FOV / blocked LOS → skip
   └─ Pick at_damage reaction
      ├─ ignore/none or AddEnemy rejected → no new state
      └─ Enemy accepted → store reaction; if calm, clear targets and change state
         └─ Holstering/disabling does not clear enemies; normal memory applies

This input assigns no wanted level directly. Existing police calls and sharing can propagate the threat.

This is the implemented SERVER tree in the local 2.5.1 implementation on dev; it does not establish a Workshop release. CLIENT receives wanted records but does not determine guilt. O is the observer, A the attacker and V the damaged target. LOS checks obstacles; the damage-witness FOV check requires the attacker to be strictly in front of the observer's eye/forward direction (including NextBot bodies).

Damage attempt
├─ Resolve siege payload owner (attacker, then inflictor) before reaction/team checks
│  └─ Vehicle resolution then follows the existing driver rules; hook order does not choose the team
├─ Shared team → no combat reaction; health damage follows bgn_team_damage
├─ Existing personal/team/mode/protection hooks may block damage
│  └─ The victim's own reaction can happen here, before health changes
└─ Positive actual damage (engine or virtual seated health)
   ├─ Invalid participant/ignored attacker, self-hit, shared team or consensual brawl → stop this notification
   ├─ Living pair (except same-team ACTOR pairs) → record first A → V, or refresh time
   │  └─ Response V → A never reverses the saved roles
   ├─ Friend mode with a player involved → keep its separate reaction override
   ├─ A already under arrest → evaluate confirmed-harm escalation first
   └─ Emit BGN_ConfirmedDamage
      ├─ Police handler → try to start/continue arrest
      ├─ Witness handler → determine a local enemy and reaction
      └─ Wanted handler → refresh an existing wanted timer

The last three items are subscribers, not a guaranteed order between hook handlers. Pair recording and existing-arrest harm checks precede that notification. Fatal hits need not create a new live-pair record; death/wanted callbacks have their own paths. See the arrest tree.

Damage witness O
├─ O is A/V, dead, too far (>2500), or cannot see A through LOS → skip
├─ A is an ACTOR outside O's FOV → skip (players/foreign entities need no FOV)
├─ Both sides share O's team → skip
├─ Neither side shares O's team, and O is not residents/police → skip
└─ Eligible witness
   ├─ If only A is a teammate, swap A/V for the resolver
   │  └─ Visibility above was checked against the actual attacker before this swap
   ├─ ResolveEnemy(O, V, A) → no choice → no new enemy/reaction for this hit
   └─ ResolveEnemy returns a side
      ├─ Protection cooldown / hook veto → no enemy
      ├─ Calm O picks ignore/none → no enemy
      └─ Choose configured reaction and request AddEnemy
         └─ Final guards can refuse: peaceful mode, team, mechanics,
            ignored entity, arrest/medic protections or another hook

For a direct resolver call, A/V are the supplied sides; the witness normalization above is not performed inside ResolveEnemy. The first matching rule wins:

Priority Condition Resolver result 1 Unsupported participant type, or ACTOR A and V share a team None. 2 Both sides are teammates of O None. 3 Only V is O's teammate A. 4 Only A is O's teammate V. 5 V is already O's enemy; A and O have no enemy-list hostility or D_HT in either direction; V is not O itself None: the common-enemy exception. 6 O is residents/police and V was first to attack A If A is a threat to O's team, choose A; otherwise choose V. 7 Player A attacks foreign NPC/NextBot V V if its available Disposition(A) is D_HT; otherwise A. 8 Foreign non-player A attacks player V A. 9 A is wanted, otherwise V is wanted A first, otherwise V. 10 O is residents/police and A was first to attack V A. 11 V is a threat to O's team, otherwise A is V first, otherwise A. Includes O's own enemy list and existing team conflict evidence. 12 ACTOR A does not list V as an enemy, otherwise ACTOR V does not list A V first, otherwise A. 13 A player participates and the pair has a saved initiator The saved initiator. 14 No rule matched None.

D_HT disables the common-enemy exception; it does not force the resolver to choose A ahead of every later rule. Existing enemy lists are never cleared by the exception. The personal victim reaction, wanted broadcasts, help and scripted enemy assignments are separate entry points, not globally filtered by this resolver.

Other ways to learn an enemy
├─ Foreign entity has direct D_HT towards a living ACTOR
│  ├─ Within 2500 + LOS, without FOV → local enemy/reaction request
│  └─ That ACTOR is residents/police → wanted request without a witness
│     (poll every second; peaceful/ignore-other-NPC modes stop the poll)
├─ CallForHelp → living teammates within 1000 who see the caller, no FOV
│  └─ Help mechanics, arrest veto, protection cooldown and AddEnemy guards still apply
├─ Periodic sharing → existing source/team/gang visibility rules
└─ Wanted broadcast / police backup → independent police notification

Initial wanted request from built-in gameplay
├─ Arrest refusal/escape/harm/kill → follow the arrest tree
├─ Completed witness phone call → report eligible known enemies
│  └─ Police already know the enemy or it is already wanted / hook veto / failed call → no new report
├─ Police radio backup → its existing conditions
└─ An ACTOR was killed
   ├─ Peaceful mode, wanted disabled, or invalid killer → stop this kill handler
   ├─ Killer is still a residents ACTOR → stop; ordinary kills do not remove this team
   ├─ Killer already wanted → refresh timer / evaluate level-up
   ├─ Killer is neither player nor ACTOR
   │  └─ Victim is residents/police → wanted, no witness required
   └─ Player / other ACTOR killer
      ├─ No other living ACTOR sees the killer with LOS + FOV within 2500 → stop
      ├─ Instant-police-kill enabled + police victim + police witness → wanted
      ├─ Enabled impunity threshold reached (>=, default 5) → wanted
      └─ Otherwise → retain the witnessed-kill count if threshold counting is enabled

New entries still pass through AddWanted exclusions for ignored/arrested entities and resident/medic actors. Assignment informs all police; it does not imply each officer witnessed the crime. Manual API calls and third-party hooks are outside this built-in trigger tree.

docs.title: Consequences of the priority order
docs.text:
Situation Current outcome Neutral gangster hits a player already in the observer's enemies No new enemy or arrest solely for this hit; player wanted status is unnecessary. Another observer without that knowledge can decide differently. The gangster is already hostile to the observer The exception is unavailable; normal resolver priorities apply. The old enemy is not forgiven. A previously protected shooter attacks an uninvolved ally Re-evaluate this new pair; the shared opponent gave no lasting immunity. A non-hostile suspect hurts the primary officer's known enemy during arrest Excluded from non-police injury/victim limits; killing still escalates separately. First-attacker memory expires It removes pair evidence, not all enemy lists or an active wanted record. Those have separate lifetimes.

Sources: api/sv_combat.lua, actor/events/sv_self_damage.lua, actor/events/sv_damage_reaction.lua, systems/sv_first_attacker_found.lua, systems/sv_relationship.lua, systems/wanted/sv_wanted_actions.lua, systems/wanted/sh_wanted_class.lua. See conflict memory for resets and arrest for weapon choice.

docs.title: Combat decisions after an enemy is accepted
docs.text:
This SERVER flow applies after the entry paths above. FSM runs the state; GOAP may plan an existing fight. Full tactic limits belong to brains.

Accepted enemy
├─ Observe all visible known enemies; share positions with original observation times
│  ├─ Hidden ordinary enemy: more than 60 s without a sighting/report → forget
│  │  └─ Engine pursuit writes do not refresh this timer; wanted/always-visible exceptions remain
│  └─ Body replaced → move position/time, combat target and recent-attacker references
├─ Select target: attacker within 5 s → siege → squad → previous target → nearest living enemy
│  ├─ Metrocop equipment uses this target; no combat enemy → arrest-target fallback
│  ├─ Hidden → last observed position / squad column; no position → stop
│  └─ Visible → combat movement; GOAP may choose cover, backup, breach or siege
├─ Police holding negotiation fire → cannot start or join siege
│  └─ Already in siege → negotiation cannot acquire its weapon capabilities
└─ Fighting with a living known enemy within 1000 inclusive
   ├─ Ordinary population recycling/respawn → blocked
   └─ NextBot HandleStuck / PullOut teleport → blocked; movement/jump attempts remain

These are cooperating state/timer paths, not a single atomic tick. They do not bypass existing state hooks or admin/death cleanup. Negotiation still uses the current radius/fear/relative-distance hostage rule, without LOS or firing-line alignment.

docs.title: Completing a police call
docs.text:
SERVER rejects a new call without a valid selected enemy or when police already know it (including an active wanted entry). Damage/protection reaction selection also checks the event's enemy before AddEnemy, so a newly reported wanted attacker cannot bypass the entry check. The reaction becomes fear.

Once calling_police has started, losing LOS, the target becoming wanted or belonging to police do not abort its 7–15 second countdown. The threat-related cancellation is distance strictly below 300 units to the selected GetEnemy() target; exactly 300 does not cancel. Allied CallForHelp can add enemy knowledge without changing the caller's state, and GOAP leaves the active call to the FSM. Missing enemies/invalid targets and disabling wanted still end the state safely. Entry limits remain: at most two callers near a player, no new call when the selected enemy is already wanted or police already know it, and wanted mode must be enabled. Completion excludes teammates before filtering enemies through police knowledge and BGN_PreCallingPolice, then normally enters fear; finishing the animation does not guarantee a new wanted entry.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
• boolean
  • Whether the actor is enabled by default in the options menu or not. 
    -- Yes
enabled = true
-- No
enabled = false

docs.title: class
docs.text:
• string | table
  • NPC entity class. May be in the form of a string or a list of strings. 
    -- string
class = 'npc_citizen'
-- table
class = {
    'npc_citizen',
    'npc_metropolice'
}

docs.title: name
docs.text:
• string
  • The name of the actor, which is displayed in the options menu.

name = 'Amogus'

docs.title: fullness
docs.text:
• number
  • Percentage filling from 0 to 100. Used when changing the slider for the total number of NPCs on the map. 
    -- number
-- If the npc limit is 30, then it will be 50% of the number 30.
fullness = 50

docs.title: limit
docs.text:
• number
  • Sets a fixed number of NPCs to spawn by default. Attention: this parameter is not compatible with "fullness". But you can still change this slider individually. 
    -- number
-- When changing the slider for the total number of NPCs, the limit will always be at a value of - 5.
limit = 5

docs.title: team
docs.text:
• table
  • Team to which the actor belongs. Default teams: residents, police, bandits, zombies. 
    -- table
-- is in the team of citizens
team = { 'residents' }
-- is a member of the citizen and police team
team = { 'residents', 'police' }

docs.title: weapons
docs.text:
• table
  • A weapon that an actor can spawn with. The weapon is not in the hands, it is "in the pocket". NPC takes (spawns) weapons if necessary.

weapons = { 'weapon_pistol', 'weapon_shotgun' }

docs.text:

-- Throw away a random amount of money from "1" to "20". If 0 falls out, then nothing will come of it.

docs.title: validator
docs.text:
• function
  • Checks the validity of the data before creating the actor. Can cancel the creation of the actor if it returns "false". 
    -- @self - config data
-- @npc_type - actor type/id
validator = function(self, npc_type)
    -- Cancels the creation of an actor if its class is not in the list of NPCs.
    if list.Get('NPC')[self.class] == nil then
        return false
    end
end,

docs.title: inherit
docs.text:
• string
  • Inherits data from another actor. Useful if you don't want to overwrite the same parameters all the time. 
    -- For example, this is our main actor.
bgNPC.cfg:SetActor('actor_1', {
    enabled = true,
    name = 'Actor 1',
    class = 'npc_citizen',
    fullness = 64,
    team = { 'residents' },
    health = 1000,
    at_random = {
        ['walk'] = 50,
        ['idle'] = 50,
    },
    at_damage = { ['defense'] = 100 },
    at_protect = { ['defense'] = 100 }
})

-- This actor uses the "inherit" parameter to borrow the missing parameters it takes from "actor_1"
bgNPC.cfg:SetActor('actor_2', {
    enabled = true,
    name = 'Actor 2',
    inherit = 'actor_1',
    team = { 'bandits' },
    at_protect = { ['fear'] = 100 },
})

-- This actor uses the "inherit" parameter to borrow missing parameters, which it takes from "actor_2", which previously borrowed data from "actor_1".
-- But there is also a team parameter where we explicitly specify from which actor we want to borrow data.
-- The "@" sign is used to indicate the actor from which we want to borrow a similar field.
bgNPC.cfg:SetActor('actor_3', {
    enabled = true,
    name = 'Actor 3',
    inherit = 'actor_2',
    team = '@actor_1',
    at_damage = { ['fear'] = 100 },
    at_protect = { ['fear'] = 100 }
})
